item.title: Refreshed Maro Itoje leads from the front as England deliver performance they needed
item.description: Moses Itoje must wonder what all the fuss was about. The newborn son of Maro and his wife had his first taste of Twickenham on Sunday afternoon, perhaps the youngest of the nearly 82,000-strong crowd at the Allianz Stadium that watched England rack up a record score against Australiia. For a player who was supposed to be resting and recharging after a gruelling physical and emotional year, one might question the wisdom of welcoming a child so close to the autumn opener. “My sleep is okay actually,” Itoje chuckled this week from the safety of England’s training base. “My wife's sleep is a bit more challenging, but she's doing a good job.” Maro Itoje (right) with his wife Mimi (left) and newborn son (Reuters) No doubt the England captain played like a man enjoying the restorative benefits of a break. It had been a bold call to allow Itoje the summer off given the juncture at which he exited, having presided over a worst-ever Six Nations. But here was a call made with long-term goals in mind . As captain of Saracens, England and the British and Irish Lions, the 32-year-old lock has been afforded precious little time off across more than a decade at Test level – indeed, his durability has counted against him, with no major injuries of which to speak. How, then, did it feel to be back pulling on an England shirt for the first time in months? “I’ve absolutely loved it. Sometimes when you have time away – and I do think it was a good thing for me personally – it just lights the fire in you a little bit. It just makes you more appreciative of the opportunity and the platform that you have when you play for England. It is something that I don’t take for granted. As many games as I have left, I want to make the absolute most of it.” Itoje was a menace throughout the game against Australia (Getty) Itoje played with that intent. Like a nosy (and noisy) neighbour peering over the fence, he timed his hassling and harrying of Ryan Lonergan superbly – getting his hands to an early box kick and up in the face of the Wallabies scrum half repeatedly. England’s captain topped the tackle charts with 16, plenty of them made before the interval in an outstanding defensive effort; at half-time, the hosts had made 75 tackles and missed just two. With plenty of focus on the battle at the breakdown, Australia were simply beaten up. Itoje and Ben Curry – influential on his return to Test duty – led the way, largely keeping their discipline as they pilfered and pawed, bar one over-balance from the England skipper. Poor Declan Meredith, the inexperienced Australia fly half, had little ball passed his way; when it did arrive, it was wobbly, and Meredith rather had the look of a seasick sailor treading an unsteady deck. “I guess they made every ruck a mess,” the captain Harry Wilson admitted. One botched late lineout where Itoje gifted Australia a try will frustrate a man of exacting standards, though the contrast between England’s last home outing against Ireland could not hav

item.title: Bundesliga Team of the Week – Matchday 9
item.description: Bundesliga Team of the Week – Matchday 9 With Matchday 9 of the 2026/27 Bundesliga season in the books, Bulinews Editor-in-Chief Rune Gjerulff has selected his Team of the Week, which lines up in a 4-3-3 formation. Goalkeeper: Marvin Schwäbe, 1. FC Köln 1. FC Köln may have lost 1-2 to local rivals Bayer Leverkusen, but Schwäbe certainly did his best to help his side take something from the game, making six saves and preventing 2.59 expected goals. Defenders: Vladimir Coufal, Hoffenheim Making his return from an injury-enforced absence, Coufal impressed by winning all of his duels while also making valuable contributions going forward. Dayot Upamecano, FC Bayern Another impressive outing from the French centre-back, who won eight duels and was excellent in possession, finding a teammate with 94 percent of his 84 passes. Koki Machida, Hoffenheim A rock-solid performance from the centre-back, who won 10 of his 11 duels while also completing 88 percent of his passes. Maximilian Mittelstädt, Stuttgart Impressed at both ends of the pitch, winning 10 duels and scoring the winner in Stuttgart's 1-0 victory over Werder Bremen. Midfielders: Joshua Kimmich, FC Bayern Named Man of the Match in Bayern's 2-1 win over Mainz, Kimmich opened the scoring and pulled the strings in midfield as usual. He completed 93 percent of his 98 passes while also winning six of his seven ground duels. Aleix Garcia, Bayer Leverkusen Leverkusen's midfield talisman scored a wonderful free-kick and completed 93 percent of his passes, while also winning six of his seven duels. Felix Nmecha, Borussia Dortmund The difference-maker for Borussia Dortmund, Nmecha scored twice to inspire his side to a 2-1 victory over SV Elversberg. Strikers: Albert Grønbæk, Hamburger SV Grønbæk made a decisive contribution with both a goal and an assist in HSV's important 3-1 win over Gladbach. Harry Kane, FC Bayern Although unable to find the net despite taking six shots, Kane impressed in a creative role, providing assists for both of Bayern's goals to take his Bundesliga assist tally to eight for the season. Brajan Gruda, RB Leipzig One of the driving forces behind RB Leipzig's 5-2 win over Augsburg, Gruda provided two assists, created five chances and completed an impressive 10 of his 11 dribbles.

item.title: Winchester City Flyers 3-3 Reading Women: Match Report
item.description: Lara Moore on the ball with Keziah Banduka (left), Ellie Szekeres (centre) and Poppy Whitburn (right) watching on / | Alison Matthews Reading Women and Winchester City Flyers played out a thrilling six-goal encounter at the Charters Community Stadium on Sunday, with the Royals having to settle for a frustrating 3-3 draw despite producing a remarkable comeback. Similar to other recent matches, the Royals found themselves on the back foot after just 10 minutes. The hosts raced into an early 2-0 lead through a headed finish from Charlie Snelling and a close-range effort from Vinnie Nkomo. However, Reading once again showed incredible resilience and character to fight their way back into the contest. Alice Curr’s eighth goal of the season began the revival before Bogi Tramontini struck to bring the Royals level – in a deserved comeback – with Reading wondering how they weren’t ahead at the break with the scores locked at 2-2. Reading continued to push after the break and were rewarded just after the hour mark when Tramontini broke through to grab her second goal of the afternoon, completing a remarkable turnaround to put the Royals 3-2 ahead. With the clock running down, Reading looked to have done enough to secure all three points, only for Flyers’ Snelling to score her second headed goal from a corner, leaving the Royals team to reflect on a hard-fought comeback, but also an ultimately frustrating and arguably disappointing 3-3 draw. I am sure that, come Tuesday morning (allowing for Ed Jackson-Norris’ 24 hours of ‘wallow time’), the focus will turn towards the positives to take from the performance, alongside addressing the areas of weakness exposed during the match. Emma Pearmine has once again assembled a competitive Winchester City Flyers side, and one that looks more than capable of challenging for the league title after finishing second in the 2025/26 campaign, just a single point behind Wycombe Wanderers. The Flyers have certainly proved to be something of a nemesis for Reading over the Royals’ last two seasons in tier five, having won all four of their previous meetings. Sunday’s draw, and disappointment at the end of the match, highlights the continued improvements and expectations of the team, with Reading finally taking points off their ‘thorn in the side’ rivals. With just four points separating the top six, the league table is already shaping up to be as competitive and closely contested as anticipated. All of the six teams will have their sights firmly set on challenging for top spot, meaning every point could prove crucial. While Sunday’s result will undoubtedly feel like two points dropped after such a determined comeback, at the end of the season, this hard-earned point against one of the league’s strongest teams may prove to be a valuable one in Reading’s promotion challenge. item.title: 'We call it war-life balance': Daryna's daily struggle to live, survive in wartime Ukraine
item.description: Daryna, 25, entered adulthood in a country at war. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion, her days have been shaped by air raid alerts, power outages and nights spent sheltering in the subway. Despite the uncertainty that shadows every day, she is determined to preserve a semblance of normal life in Kyiv. FRANCE 24 met a young woman who has become emblematic of a generation learning to live under daily bombardment.

item.title: African players in Europe: Jackson scores as Villa squander leads at United
item.description: Senegal star Nicolas Jackson scored after just four minutes for Aston Villa, who twice surrendered two-goal leads in a remarkable 4-4 Premier League draw away to Manchester United at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) Jackson put his side 2-0 ahead against United, but it wasn’t enough to inspire a victory at Old Trafford. When Jackson tapped in after United goalkeeper Senne Lammens palmed the ball into his path, it appeared the 25-year-old’s ninth goal in 14 games in all competitions this term would be the spark for a comfortable Villa win. But in an incredible finale, United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue a draw. YANN GBOHO (Coventry City) The Ivory Coast winger scored his first Premier League goal in a 3-1 defeat at Everton. Gboho, signed from French side Toulouse in September, put Coventry ahead with a composed finish after evading slack defending in the 52nd minute. But Frank Lampard’s team crumbled after the 25-year-old’s strike as Everton scored three times to leave the visitors one point above the relegation zone. SPAIN YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander) Moroccan forward Zabiri continued his superb season with another goal to help Santander win 2-1 at Malaga. The 21-year-old bagged his ninth of the campaign with a simple finish to tuck a rebound home into the empty net. Only Raphinha, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal have scored more goals this season in La Liga. ITALY KONAN N’DRI (Lecce) After Angolan Kailonda Gaspar conceded a 60th-minute own goal to give Torino the lead in a clash of bottom-half Serie A clubs, Niger international N’Dri scored to salvage a 1-1 draw for visiting Lecce. The architect of the equaliser was Mali international Lassana Coulibaly. GERMANY EZECHIEL BANZUZI (RB Leipzig) Banzuzi’s goal proved the turning point as he kick-started Leipzig’s recovery to beat Augsburg 5-2 at home in the Bundesliga after conceding inside the opening minute. Anton Kade had Augsburg in front after 36 seconds but Banzuzi levelled in the 33rd minute when he turned a Brajan Gruda pass into the bottom right corner. The 21-year-old Democratic Republic of Congo internnational has two goals and two assists in the league this season. UCHENNA OGUNDU (Augsburg) Ogundu’s first goal in Augsburg colours was a mere consolation as his side crashed at Leipzig. With Leipzig 5-1 up, Augsburg’s Alexis Claude Maurice intercepted the ball and sent his side in the other direction. Fabian Rieder latched on to Claude Maurice’s pass before finding Ogundu, who slid the ball into the bottom corner. FRANCE LASSINE SINAYOKO (Paris FC) Ligue 1’s leading scorer Sinayoko netted after 63 minutes to give third-placed Paris FC a 1-0 win at lowly Auxerre. It was the ninth goal of the campaign in 10 matches for the Mali striker. The post African players in Europe: Jackson scores as Villa squander leads at United appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Journalist explains how Bernardo Silva is becoming Real Madrid’s new midfield conductor: ‘He isn’t Modric, but…’
item.description: Journalist explains how Bernardo Silva is becoming Real Madrid’s new midfield conductor: ‘He isn’t Modric, but…’ Bernardo Silva is gradually establishing himself as an important figure in Real Madrid’s midfield, with his performances attracting praise from journalist Mario Cortegana. The Portuguese midfielder arrived with considerable expectations, particularly because of the experience and technical quality he could bring to a team searching for greater creativity and control in possession. Although comparisons with Luka Modric were inevitable, Cortegana says the Portuguese is developing a different role under Jose Mourinho. Speaking on his YouTube channel , Cortegana highlighted the midfielder’s ability to connect Real Madrid’s different departments and give direction to their attacking play. Why Bernardo Silva is important to Real Madrid Bernardo was initially viewed as an experienced addition capable of addressing Real Madrid’s midfield shortcomings. Bernardo Silva is slowly finding his rhythm at Real Madrid. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) However, his arrival was not universally convincing, particularly with fans expecting the club to pursue a more traditional creative midfielder such as Rodri or Martin Zubimendi. Nevertheless, Cortegana believes the Portuguese international is gradually demonstrating why his signing makes sense. “Bernardo Silva isn’t Modric, but without being brilliant, he’s weaving Real Madrid’s football together to give it meaning; his partnership with Tchouaméni is really taking hold.” Bernardo’s partnership with Tchouameni improves Madrid’s midfield One of Bernardo’s most important contributions has been his developing relationship with Aurelien Tchouameni , which comes after Mourinho has decided to use Federico Valverde in defence. The Frenchman provides defensive protection and physical presence, while Bernardo offers the technical qualities needed to progress possession and connect attacks. Bernardo has benefited from Valverde’s move to the right-back spot. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Cortegana specifically highlighted the Portuguese midfielder’s influence on Madrid’s build-up, explaining that “Bernardo makes passes, makes runs off the ball, and gives meaning to the game with those small details. “Neither Tchouameni, nor Fede Valverde, nor Camavinga have that ability to build play.” Modric comparisons explain Bernardo’s growing influence Replacing Luka Modric was never going to be straightforward for the player nor for Real Madrid. The Croatian’s technical quality, vision and influence over several successful Real Madrid teams established an exceptionally high standard. Hence, Bernardo should not be judged against Modric’s entire career, although there are similarities in the way both players help organise possession and provide direction when their teams need greater control.

item.title: Gary Neville singles out FOUR players who will get Manchester United relegated after defensive disaster against Aston Villa
item.description: Manchester United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United legend Gary and Phil Neville have delivered a scathing assessment of the club’s current defensive options following a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. The former stars believe the lack of recruitment in the backline has left the Red Devils in a perilous position that could threaten their top-flight status. Chaotic eight-goal thriller at Old Trafford United went into the November international break sitting 18th in the Premier League after a disastrous defensive display. The hosts found themselves two goals down within five minutes courtesy of rapid strikes from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson. Michael Carrick's men rallied before the break, drawing level through a Bruno Fernandes penalty and a goal from former Villa midfielder Youri Tielemans. However, the visitors regained control after the restart with a Josh McGinn penalty and a fourth from Leon Goretzka. Staring at a damaging defeat, United salvaged a point in injury time. Substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu struck late on to secure a 4-4 draw , sparing the club from dropping to the bottom of the table. Neville brothers blast defensive options The match ended with a makeshift backline consisting of Noussair Mazraoui, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven, and Dorgu. Speaking on NBC Sports , Gary Neville pointed to the club's summer transfer activity as the root cause of the chaos. "The reason Manchester United have conceded four goals is because they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window," he said. "Every one knew they had to do that, they needed defenders. The current ones are making mistake after mistake after mistake. The defenders that finished that game will get you relegated. Watch the defensive errors… we all screamed in the transfer window that they have to bring some defenders in. They had to bring the transfer budget forward and bring defenders in." His brother Phil shared the same sentiment, singling out the closing defensive quartet. "The back-four that finished the game - Mazraoui, Yoro, Heaven and Dorgu - that gets you relegated," he added. "That back-four gets you the sack as a manager and that back-four cannot keep United, I don’t think, in the Premier League. That back-four gets you relegated, it’s poor. It’s not good enough to play in the Premier League." Deep-rooted institutional problems The draw leaves United suffering an eight-game winless league run, plunging them to their lowest position at this stage of a campaign since 1986. Despite this grim reality, Neville insists that sacking Carrick would not solve the wider systemic issues at Old Trafford. "You can paper over the cracks and get a new manager bounce," the former captain added. "When the new manager comes in, everybody’s happy for a couple of months and all of a sudden, six months later, it happens again. item.title: PSG drop Ibrahim Maza pursuit
item.description: PSG drop Ibrahim Maza pursuit Paris Saint-Germain have completely dropped their pursuit of Bayer Leverkusen forward Ibrahim Maza (20), as per a report from Sacha Tavolieri. The Algerian had been touted as a potential January recruit. Dipping into the transfer window is an option at PSG’s disposal this winter as they look to replace Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. The Georgian suffered an ACL injury earlier this month and may not play again this season. There are plenty of ways to replace ‘Kvara’ internally, but Luis Enrique has not ruled out signing a player, should an opportunity arise. Maza is not a possibility that will be explored. In opening talks with his PSG, the player’s father wished to go though an intermediary in the form of Stellar. It was a means of “checking” PSG’s interest, Tavolieri understands, but it is a move that has not been perceived well by Luís Campos, who has put an end to any pursuit. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: ‘Held My Breath For a Second,’ ‘We Can’t Have Anything Good’ — NFL World Taken Aback By Footage of Eagles LB’s Nasty Hit on J.J. McCarthy
item.description: ‘Held My Breath For a Second,’ ‘We Can’t Have Anything Good’ — NFL World Taken Aback By Footage of Eagles LB’s Nasty Hit on J.J. McCarthy The New York Giants picked up a 19-11 win against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, with J.J. McCarthy leading the team at quarterback. McCarthy faced constant pressure from the Eagles’ defense, which brought him down for five sacks. Notably, McCarthy’s performance was also interrupted by a frightening moment in the third quarter. He took a brutal hit to his lower abdomen in the third quarter when Eagles linebacker Zack Baun led with his helmet while attempting to stop the QB’s run. It ultimately made direct contact with McCarthy’s side as Baun brought him down, triggering reactions from the NFL community. J.J. McCarthy’s Painful Collision With Zack Baun Leaves the NFL World Worried After the brutal play, McCarthy attempted a few warm-up throws to determine whether he could continue. He winced in pain after his first attempt and collapsed to the ground in considerable discomfort following the second. The medical staff later escorted McCarthy to the locker room for further evaluation. Reacting to the footage, KDKA-TV sports director Bob Pompeani compared the collision to a similar incident involving Mike Tomczak and Tracy Scroggins. “J. J. McCarthy turned into a massive hit. It reminded me of Mike Tomczak turning into Tracy Scroggins and getting blindsided in a 1995 game. Tomczak suffered a bruised sternum,” Pompeani wrote . “Dang,” popular analyst/ host Trey Wingo wrote . McCarthy later explained that the play was designed as a quarterback run, but his decision to pull the ball back inside after reading the defense left him exposed to Baun. He acknowledged that he spotted the linebacker late and attempted to lower his shoulder to absorb the contact, but failed to get low enough. McCarthy also credited Baun for delivering an excellent hit and accepted responsibility, saying that he needed to do a better job of protecting himself in such situations. Meanwhile, reactions to the hit continued. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer “JJ McCarthy ran into a WALL on this one. Held my breath for a second,” Anthony Rivardo, host of the Fireside Giants, wrote . “The guy is just so small, man… naturally, the first non-scramble rushing attempt he has as a starter ends in him leaving the game. We can’t have anything good. Not one thing,” Justin Penik, host of the “Talkin’ Giants” podcast, wrote . McCarthy managed to return to the game just before the end of the third quarter and remained optimistic about his condition, insisting he would be fine. But his recovery could become a concern for the Giants, who are scheduled to face the Washington Commanders on Thursday. With McCarthy initially listed as questionable to return, the Giants turned to Jameis Winston under center. Winston, who ranks No. 23 in the PFN QB Impact with a 70.5 grade, led the offense on a touchdown drive before returning to the sideline.

item.title: Chiefs’ Harrison Butker admits ‘booing myself’ amid fan frustration
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Chiefs’ Harrison Butker admits ‘booing myself’ amid fan frustration appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Kansas City Chiefs secured another win on Sunday, but their kicking struggles continued to cause concern. Harrison Butker missed two field goals in the first half against the New York Jets, drawing loud boos from the home crowd at Arrowhead Stadium. The veteran kicker acknowledged the fans’ frustration after Kansas City’s 35-12 victory and admitted he has been just as critical of himself. “I’m booing myself sometimes. People are passionate. The fans are passionate. They want to win games. They want me to make kicks. I want to make kicks. It’s part of it. That’s what you sign up for, and I’ve got to be better,” Butker said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) #Chiefs K Harrison Butker speaks following another game with a missed FG. When asked about boos heard in the home crowd, he told @SSJWHB , “I’m booing myself sometimes. People are passionate, the fans are passionate. They want to win games. They want me to make kicks. I want to… pic.twitter.com/yDtsiNmL1g — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) November 8, 2026 His latest misses came on attempts from 56 and 51 yards. The first kick went wide right, but a Jets penalty gave him another opportunity from closer range. Butker missed that attempt as well, leaving Kansas City with a 14-12 halftime lead. The misses added to a difficult stretch for the 31-year-old. He has struggled over his previous four appearances, prompting the Chiefs to bring Justin Tucker onto their practice squad to provide competition. Head coach Andy Reid did not offer a decision on Butker’s future after Sunday’s game . “I’ll look at everything. I’m not making any decisions right now today,” Reid said. Butker, meanwhile, maintained that he remains confident despite the results. “I feel confident. I’m excited for the kicks, and I just have to do better,” he said. Kansas City eventually pulled away with 21 unanswered points in the second half to improve to 6-2. However, Butker’s struggles remain an issue the Chiefs will need to address before their next game against the Atlanta Falcons. item.title: UConn women's basketball honors Azzi Fudd for lasting impact on program
item.description: STORRS — As highlights flickered across the video board and the crowd at Gampel Pavilion rose to its feet, Azzi Fudd paused beneath the championship banners she helped add to the rafters, soaking in the cheers one more time. The former UConn star smiled, waved and embraced those closest to her on Sunday afternoon. Fudd was back at center stage in Storrs , only this time not as a player chasing history, but as the newest member of the Huskies of Honor. Just two seasons removed from helping UConn capture a national championship, Fudd was honored just before the Huskies’ game against Iowa. Former Huskies Alisha Clark, Gabby Williams, Tina Charles and Tiffany Hayes were all in attendance. Despite battling injuries throughout her college career, Fudd completed her time at Storrs as one of the program’s defining players. Her induction into the Huskies of Honor solidifies her legacy as one of UConn’s most storied players. Sarah Strong sparks UConn: UConn women’s basketball gets the response it needed from Sarah Strong vs Iowa UConn vs Iowa takeaways: UConn women’s basketball vs Iowa | Biggest takeaways from Huskies’ win Fudd hopes her story can inspire the next generation of basketball players who have hopes of reaching the heights she has. “I hope that they can look up to me the way I look up to all the other names up here,” Fudd said before Sunday’s game. “I hope they can look at my time and see how imperfect it was and have that as inspiration and as a motivation when something goes wrong.” Few players arrived at UConn with the hype that Fudd had. The Virginia native was the No. 1 recruit in the country in the class of 2021 and was one of the most accomplished prospects to enter the program. Fudd was a Gatorade National Player of the Year and a Naismith High School Player of the Year, getting offers from all the top schools in the country. Fudd chose UConn over the likes of UCLA, Texas and Oregon. She was viewed as the next great star in a lineage that included Maya Moore, Breanna Stewart and Diana Taurasi. But Fudd’s path in Storrs was rarely linear. Injuries repeatedly interrupted her career. She missed time as a freshman with a foot injury, battled nagging knee issues as a sophomore and suffered a torn ACL and meniscus just two games into the 2023-24 season. What was supposed to be a career of dominance became a test of resilience. Rather than letting her injuries define her, the setbacks became part of the legacy she left behind. In her senior year, Fudd, along with Paige Bueckers, helped UConn win its 12 th national championship. In her fifth year, Fudd started all 39 games and helped the Huskies get back to the Final Four, averaging a career-high 17.3 points per game en route to earning All-American honors. By the time her career was over, Fudd had amassed nearly 1,700 points and was among the winningest players in program history. “There were so many obstacles, so many ups, so many downs, so many unknowns, so many injuries,” Fudd said. “There

item.title: Halling, 200 freestyle relay team qualifies for state finals
item.description: OTSEGO — The Sturgis swim and dive team had a strong showing at the conference finals this past weekend. Sturgis finished third overall as a team at the SCC Conference Meet hosted by the Otsego Aquatic Center. The Trojans finished with 296 points. Harper Creek won the conference finals while piling up 555 points at the event. South Haven finished just ahead of Sturgis in third with 324. The good news for Sturgis was a pair of state-qualifying swims. MUSICAL TIME: 'Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat' coming to Sturgis VOLLEYBALL ENDS: Volleyball seasons end for Sturgis, Three Rivers in district play Katelyn Halling registered an individual state cut in the 50 freestyle on Friday. She posted 25.83 seconds in that race. On Saturday, she finished third in the 50 free final at 26.08 seconds, that also would have been a state time. Halling also helped Sturgis qualify for the state finals in the 200 freestyle relay. The team had been attempting go log a state cut in that race all season. It finally came on their last attempt as they posted a time of 1:46.60 to finish second overall at the conference finals. Halling teamed up with Sydney Herblet, Lilly Whitehead and Ainsley Gump in that race. Sturgis finished with several all-conference swims on the weekend. Gump won the 200 individual medley race at 2:13.69. The 200 medley relay team of Brooklyn Draper, Whitehead, Gump and Halling swam to second place overall at 1:58.19. Sturgis also had a consolation finalist time of 2:45.31 with the team of Chiara Guiduzzi, Makenna Holden, Haylee Trine and Nele Strasen swimming to 16th. Herblet finished fourth overall in the 200 freestyle race at 2:12.76. Mia Feyes took home ninth at 2:20.78. In the 200 IM, Draper swam to ninth at 2:33.77. For the 50 freestyle, Whitehead was 10th at 27.81 seconds, Ella Whitehead finished 13th at 28.80. Ava Albarran posted 1:27.22 for 15th in the 100 butterfly. The 100 freestyle saw Halling finish fifth at 59.22 seconds. In the lengthy 500 freestyle, Herblet came in fifth place overall at 5:56.04. The Sturgis team of Draper, Albarran, Feyes and Ella Whitehead swam to seventh in the 200 freestyle relay. That group posted a time of 1:56.31. In 100 backstroke racing, Feyes earned an all-conference time of 1:15.75 for eighth place. The 100 breaststroke race saw Gump finish second at 1:09.11, Lilly Whitehead was third overall with a time of 1:14.51 and Ella Whitehead was sixth overall at 1:16.47. Sturgis earned an all-conference swim in the 400 freestyle relay. The team of Ella Whitehead, Albarran, Feyes and Herblet clocked a time of 4:26.23 to finish eighth. The Trojans will be well represented at the MHSAA swimming finals next weekend. A preview story on the participants and their races will appear online later this week and in print on Saturday. item.title: Oviedo sack Calero: Raúl González will be the new manager
item.description: Oviedo sack Calero: Raúl González will be the new manager Not even Real Oviedo’s victory at the Nuevo Mirandilla was enough to save Julián Calero. Despite taking three points against Cádiz and putting Oviedo firmly in the hunt for the promotion play-off places, Grupo Pachuca has decided to part ways with him. In his place, the Asturian club’s majority shareholder has turned to Raúl González Blanco to take charge and lead the push for promotion to the top flight, following the end of his spell with Real Madrid’s academy and reserve team. Calero’s future was already hanging by a thread before the trip to Cádiz following two particularly painful setbacks. The first came in the Copa del Rey, where Numancia (from the Segunda Federación) knocked the Blues out on penalties after a 3-3 draw that exposed serious defensive weaknesses. Days later, defeat to UD Las Palmas at the Carlos Tartiere shattered what confidence remained. The victory over Cádiz was not enough to restore the board’s faith. Jesús Martínez made the coach’s dismissal official on Monday, paving the way for Raúl’s new project. For the Real Madrid legend, this opportunity marks his first managerial role in professional football after his lengthy development spell at La Fábrica and in charge of Real Madrid Castilla. item.title: Auto racing - Lime Rock Park announces 2027 major events schedule
item.description: The schedule for eight major racing and car events in 2027 has been released by Lime Rock Park in Lakeville, Connecticut, set to celebrate its 70th anniversary. Lime Rock has been a prime 1.5-mile road racing course since 1957 and regularly hosts professional and amateur racing events and shows. The United States Auto Club Mustang Cup will lead off on May 14-15 (with free admission) followed by the Trans Am Memorial Day Classic from May 27-30 — also taking place are the American V8s, SVRA Invitational, International GT and Prototype America, plus Royals Garage Car Show. The Sports Car Club of America New England Regionals will be hosted June 11-12 (the first day is free). The summer schedule begins with the LIUNA 150 NASCAR FedEx Freight Truck Series and ARCA Menards Series weekend on July 9-10. The Gridlife Circuit Legends will appear Aug. 20-21. The Labor Day weekend will have the Historic Festival 45 from Sept. 2-6 - in 2026, 287 competition entries and 1,200 vehicles took part. The Friday, Saturday and Monday cards feature vintage racing, and Sunday in the Park features the Lime Rock Concourse and Gathering of the Marques showcase. The fall schedule will have the FCP Euro Northeast Grand Prix event for IMSA on Sept. 23-25. The MiataCon will take place Oct. 29-30, celebrating Mazda's MX-5 roadster — more than 1,100 Miatas took part in the 2026 event. Tickets go on sale on Monday, Nov. 9, with season passes and Insiders Club passes available for purchase. The track announces general admission ticket prices for the major events remain unchanged from 2026 and reduced gate admission for the Trans Am Memorial Day Classic. "Celebrating 70 years of Lime Rock Park is an incredible milestone, and we're entering this anniversary season with tremendous momentum,'' said Dicky Riegel, the Park President and CEO. "The growth we've experienced across our major events, particularly with grassroots motorsports and enthusiast driven weekends, speaks to the passion of our fans and the strength of the motorsports community. With an expanded schedule, the return of IMSA and our commitment to keeping events accessible and affordable, we're looking forward to making our 70th season one to remember.'' Additional events will be released at a later date. Middletown, in the heart of Orange County, is 50 miles from Lime Rock, and Poughkeepsie is 38 miles away. White Plains is 60 miles away, and Binghamton is 90 miles. Go to: LimeRock.com; Tixr.com/groups/limerock kmcmillan@th-record.com X / Twitter: @KenMcMillanTHR This article originally appeared on Times Herald-Record: Auto racing - Lime Rock Park announces 2027 major events schedule

item.title: Four Lenawee County runners earn all-state honors in cross country finals at MIS
item.description: BROOKLYN — Adrian runners Ayda Skeels and Madison Petty have been two of Lenawee County’s fastest all season long. On Saturday, Adrian’s dynamic duo represented the best of Lenawee County at the MHSAA Cross Country Championships by earning all-state honors with their performances in the Division 2 girls race at Michigan International Speedway. “This whole season we’ve just been able to push each other in workouts and races,” Skeels said about her teammate. “It’s really awesome for me to have that person.” Skeels finished 15th, while Petty placed 25th. “I just wanted to run my own race and compete with the other girls around me,” Skeels said. “Overall, just to finish top 15, I’m pretty happy with that.” Two other Lenawee County runners earned all-state honors with top-30 performances at the state meet, both from Blissfield. item.title: Relieved Cristian Chivu hails Inter’s resilience after surviving brutal 27-day marathon
item.description: FC Internazionale v Como 1907 - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Inter head coach Cristian Chivu has expressed his pride in his squad’s resilience following a convincing 2-0 victory over Como at San Siro. The Nerazzurri boss admitted his relief at navigating a punishing schedule that saw his side compete in nine fixtures over a span of just 27 days. Overcoming a relentless schedule Chivu has offered a candid assessment of his team’s physical state after they navigated a daunting fixture list. The Nerazzurri secured a vital three points on Sunday, ensuring they remain firmly in the hunt at the top of the Serie A table. The result provided much-needed relief for a squad that has been pushed to its absolute limits over the past month. The manager admitted that while the level of performance fluctuated, the primary objective was simply to survive the marathon and remain competitive in all competitions. Reflecting on the grueling period, Chivu highlighted the sheer volume of football his players have endured. "I'd start by mentioning the fact that we’ve had nine games in 27 days, which has taken a lot of energy and brought lots of ups and downs. We always want to try and improve, but sometimes you have to swallow your pride and just work hard and prepare with the right mentality for the next games in front of you," he explained to Sky Sport Italia . Tactical discipline secures victory The win against Como was built on a blistering start, with the hosts establishing a commanding lead early in the contest. Precision in the final third allowed Inter to dictate the tempo and eventually take the sting out of the game. Chivu was particularly pleased with how his tactical instructions were executed by the players from the opening whistle at San Siro. "Today, we raised the pace and intensity and our preparation served us well in terms of quality and pressure. We played as a team. We did well in the first half from all points of view, and then sometimes you need to know how to manage other moments of the game. I congratulate the boys, who were wonderful today," Chivu added. Moving past derby disappointment For Inter, the victory was also about exorcising the demons of a painful defeat in the Milan derby. Bouncing back from such a high-profile setback was essential for maintaining morale within the dressing room. Chivu insisted that dwelling on past failures was not an option for a club with Inter's lofty ambitions for the current campaign. "There’s always room for improvement. You can’t always have everything and be perfect every time. You have to accept that the season is long and there are lots and lots of games," he remarked. The coach praised his players for their mental fortitude, stating, "We lost the derby, but we had to move forwards. We have to pull in the same direction and carry on in what is a big and ambitious season." item.title: The Scott Stecher standard is brave new world for Woodmore football
item.description: You don't want to be the group that doesn't go 10-0. That's what assistant coach Seth Dufendock meant when he reminded Woodmore players that was now the standard. The departing seniors helped make sure of it, before a 28-0 setback to visiting Delta in the second round of the postseason in Division VI. Woodmore, which had never hosted a game in the playoffs, was unbeaten in the regular season for the first time since 1995 and second time in program history. It had a first-round bye after winning the Sandusky Bay Conference championship for the first league crown since 1997. High school football Woodmore football eliminated in second round of OHSAA postseason The Wildcats were 2-8 three years ago, before coach Scott Stecher's arrival. They were 5-5 and 7-4, including a postseason setback his first two seasons. The response from the community warms Stecher's heart. "It brought football back to a place where Friday nights here are a happening," he said. "This hasn't been done in 30 years — all this stuff. We want to keep it rolling." Stecher felt embraced from the start. He wasn't sure he'd get another chance at a program's helm, after his final year at Monroeville in 2020. He was then an assistant at a few stops before Woodmore. "It means the world to me," he said. "It makes me more a believer that God puts you where he wants you. Being part of a football family again has been an awesome blessing. Seeing the kids grow and the community pride." This iteration was the most selfless team Stecher has ever coached. "These kids are high character, good kids," he said. "We had to get them a little meaner, tougher. They're loving, caring. The servant leadership was outstanding teaching young kids. That brought them this far. This group cares about each other." Sophomore running back/linebacker Lucas Caldwell isn't the only one who is already anxious to try to uphold the standard next season. The returners will be a little more battle tested and got a taste of what it takes in Week 12. "He's a one of a kind football player, and his character," Stecher said. "He's fun to be around. I look forward to it." Maybe they'll establish another standard by winning a home playoff game. "We'll work so much harder to do everything we can to be better than this year," Caldwell said. "Knowing the guys that are leaving, they did so much for us. We have to do more every year." mhorn@gannett.com 419-307-4892 X: @MatthewHornNH This article originally appeared on Fremont News-Messenger: The Scott Stecher standard is brave new world for Woodmore football

item.title: Trump says Iran war ‘highly unlikely’ to resume
item.description: US President Donald Trump cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN it was “highly unlikely,” ahead of a meeting with mediator Qatar’s prime minister on Monday. Trump has threatened to resume strikes in recent weeks, with US media reports suggesting that hostilities could restart after last Tuesday’s midterm elections. The president told CNN in an interview on Sunday that renewed fighting was “highly unlikely,” but warned that his decision “depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement.” “I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them,” he said. Trump is scheduled to meet Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who is also the country’s foreign minister, at the White House on Monday. The meeting will be Trump’s first with a foreign leader since a massive midterm loss that saw his Republican Party lose control of Congress. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested on Sunday that peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the vote was being assessed. “For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone,” Araghchi told state television. “We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward,” he added. – ‘They had enough’ – Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran — which began with US-Israeli strikes in late February — was at least partially responsible for the Republicans’ defeat. Araghchi said Monday that the US president “clearly recognizes that the vast majority of Americans are disgusted with Israel.” “Americans are evidently sick and tired of Israel bamboozling US administrations into Forever Wars,” Araghchi said on X. “They had enough. So has our region.” In Sunday’s CNN interview, Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting the United States’ terms. “They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 percent inflation,” Trump claimed. “They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off.” Iran’s official figures put inflation at nearly 90 percent year-on-year in September. Iranian state television said the island of Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz was attacked overnight Sunday, hours after the official IRNA news agency reported two explosions there. Various regional powers, including Qatar and Pakistan, have been trying for months without success to bring a definitive halt to the war. Outright fighting has largely subsided, but Iran continues in its efforts to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, vital to global energy supplies, while the US Navy maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. The post Trump says Iran war ‘highly unlikely’ to resume appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Who is Alice Huang, Chinese exec accused of spying on Nvidia CEO?
item.description: Tech executive Alice Huang is the woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Jensen Huang, head of US artificial intelligence chip titan Nvidia, according to media reports. Public details are sparse about the woman, also known as Huang Le, who had reportedly been a top figure at a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed International. Here is what we know about her and the company: – Who is Alice Huang? – Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia boss, according to the New York Times, which first reported that Jensen Huang was the alleged target of a spy plot. Despite their shared surname, Alice Huang is no relation to the 63-year-old Taiwanese-born head of the world’s most valuable company. The Times, citing people briefed on the surveillance, said that Alice Huang speaks good English and is well connected at the highest level of the global AI chip industry. The sector is highly sensitive as the United States and China race to develop advanced AI systems with potential military applications. An online search brought up a short profile for Alice Huang, with her photo, on a Chinese fund database. It listed previous jobs including at HSBC bank, and as a reporter for Chinese media outlets CCTV and Hunan TV. AFP was unable to verify the contents of the profile, or who had written it, but has attempted to contact the companies cited. – How are the pair connected? – Media reports last week said they had a close relationship, and Jensen Huang told Nvidia employees on Sunday he was “deeply sorry” for being “unfaithful to my wife”. One photo from an industry party in 2024, posted on LinkedIn, appears to show the leather jacket-clad Nvidia boss sitting next to a long-haired woman in glitzy jewellery believed to be Alice Huang. The following year, they both attended a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. Alice Huang is also seen following the Nvidia chief as he re-enters the restaurant after talking to journalists outside, running her fingers down his lower back. They later leave the restaurant in the same car. – What is Megaspeed? – US officials concluded last year that Alice Huang was targeting Jensen Huang as a spy, according to the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal. At the time, Alice Huang was said to be a top executive at data centre firm Megaspeed International, which rents out computing power to other companies to train and run AI. item.title: Gunmen kill security operative, three others in Plateau attack
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed three residents and a security operative during an attack on Bel village in Sho community, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, while several other persons sustained injuries. The attack reportedly occurred at about 9 p.m. on Sunday when the gunmen stormed the community and opened fire on residents. A resident of the community, Mr Bulus Bot, who confirmed the incident, said the attackers invaded the village at night and shot indiscriminately at innocent citizens. “The gunmen stormed the community at about 9 p.m. and opened fire on innocent citizens, leaving some people dead and others injured,” he said. Bot described the incident as a disturbing attack on the community, noting that residents were caught up in the violence when the gunmen opened fire. He said some persons sustained injuries during the attack, adding to the concern among residents over the safety of people in the area. The Publicity Secretary of Berom Youth Moulders Association, Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the killings and identified three of the victims as Emmanuel Pam Dachung, 15; Joseph Gyang, 28; and Emmanuel Yohanna, 32. He alleged that a soldier was also among those killed in the attack, bringing the reported death toll to four. Tengwong condemned the attack, describing the killing of innocent residents as unacceptable, and called on security operatives to track down those responsible. He urged security agencies to ensure that the perpetrators were identified and brought to justice, stressing the need for decisive action to prevent further attacks on communities in the area. Efforts to get a reaction from security operatives on the attack were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Gunmen kill security operative, three others in Plateau attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: WIMBIZ: ‘I learnt business from my mother’ – Tony Elumelu champions women’s economic leadership
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Billionaire businessman Tony Elumelu has credited his mother with teaching him the fundamentals of business, using her experience as a small restaurant owner to emphasise the importance of women’s economic leadership and participation in Africa’s development. Elumelu said his earliest lessons in entrepreneurship, including risk management, cash flow, customer relations, discipline and resilience, came from watching his mother build a business and provide for her family. Elumelu, who spoke on Friday at the 25th Annual Conference of Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ), held at Eko Hotel and Suites, Victoria Island, Lagos, recalled how his mother’s hard work shaped his understanding of business. “I did not start with capital. I started with a mother, a mother who ran a small restaurant and worked harder than anyone I’ve ever known. “I watched her turn very little into a living, and a living into a future for our children. That was my first business school,” he said. He added that his understanding of the practical demands of running a business came from observing her daily experiences. “My first lesson in risk, in cash flow, in customers, in discipline, in hard work, in resilience, in getting up the next morning when the day before had gone very badly, came all from her, a woman,” he said. Drawing from that experience, the chairman of Heirs Holdings argued that women’s participation in business and economic leadership was not simply a matter of fairness but a necessity for Africa’s competitiveness. “Women’s economic leadership is not a concession to fairness. It is a requirement for competitiveness,” he said. Elumelu disclosed that 48 per cent of the 24,633 entrepreneurs supported by the Tony Elumelu Foundation over 15 years were women. According to him, the foundation has disbursed more than $120 million in seed capital to entrepreneurs across all 54 African countries, helping them create more than 1.5 million jobs and generate over $4.2 billion in revenue. He urged African leaders and business owners to provide women with greater access to funding and opportunities to lead businesses, insisting that the continent could not achieve inclusive prosperity by undervaluing half of its talent. Beyond women’s participation in the economy, Elumelu identified unreliable electricity, inadequate value creation and shortage of capital as three major obstacles standing between Africa and its economic prosperity. Speaking on the conference theme, “Rooted, Rising, Ready: Born in Africa, Built for the World,” he described electricity as a critical requirement for industrialisation and technological development, arguing that African countries could not fully embrace emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence without reliable power. “We cannot talk about AI without fixing electricity. It is not possible. If we fix electricity, Africa will take off,” he said. On value creation, he challenged African countries to m

item.title: Dev error bricked 600 PCs, caused $1M CD-ROM write-off
item.description: Welcome to Monday, the day upon which The Register offers a new instalment of " Who, Me? " – our reader-contributed column that shares your stories of messing up, 'fessing up, and somehow finding redress. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Oriel" who told us he once worked for a vendor of small business accounting software. This story comes from a time when software shipped on CD-ROMs and users bought it off the shelf in actual shops. The vendor released a new version each year and always shipped it before a major holiday that's celebrated with a giant meal. Oriel was part of the team whose job it was to get the package ready on time. In the previous year, they flubbed the job because the program didn't always install itself on some PCs running Windows 95 or Windows ME machines system due to registry corruption. "We wanted to increase our successful installation metrics, so in conjunction with the installation team, a key decision was made – by me – to force the updating of registry keys to enable the install," Oriel admitted. In his email to The Register , he asked the portentous question: "What could possibly go wrong?" What went wrong was that not long after the software was shipped, the vendor's support lines started getting calls from customers who complained that after installing the accounting package none of their other software would work. "Installing a new version of our application had borked the customer's machine completely," Oriel wrote. The company decided the best thing to do was to tell affected customers they should go and buy a new PC – and that it would pick up the bill, no questions asked. "In the week prior to the holiday, we replaced over 600 machines," Oriel told The Register . Oriel and his developer colleagues were of course told to fix the problem but couldn't reproduce it nor figure out their mistake. "To get a reproduction case we need a user's machine where the user had created a Windows Registry restore point prior to installing our application," Oriel explained. If the developers could find such a machine, the plan was to roll it back to the restore point, verify everything was in order before the customer installed the update, install the accounting software, and figure out the problem. The company tasked its support agents with finding a customer willing to surrender their PC, which proved difficult because few bothered to create a registry restore point. The day before the holiday, a customer volunteered their machine. This customer was located a few hours away by road, so an engineer got the job of visiting on the morning of the holiday to pick up the stricken machine, give the customer a shiny new system and configure it to their specifications. Said engineer did the job, which took so long he was invited to stay for the holiday meal, then returned to HQ with the broken box. item.title: Nvidia announces probe into Huang amid reports China spied on him
item.description: Chip giant Nvidia’s board announced Sunday it had opened a probe into chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence. Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials concluded that Alice Huang, a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data center company called Megaspeed, had been funnelling information to Beijing. The executive, also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang, developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said. In a message to company employees released Sunday, the Nvidia chief acknowledged having an affair and apologized to his family and company staff. “I was unfaithful to my wife,” he said. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Jensen Huang is a huge figure in the artificial intelligence revolution and a close informal adviser to US President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly spoken out against regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand in the AI race. The Times said Alice Huang’s relationship with the Nvidia chief could have given her insights into Trump’s thinking around AI. The issue of AI is likely to arise during Trump’s planned talks with President Xi Jinping later this month at a summit in China. Asked whether the Nvidia chief would be joining the president’s trip to Asia, which includes the Asia-Pacific summit in China’s Shenzhen on Sunday, Trump told reporters: “I don’t know but I’ll certainly take him.” Trump said Huang was “a fine person, but you never know what’s going on. I’m sure — I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job.” – ‘Speculation’ – Nvidia said in a statement it had opened an independent probe “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The statement added: “While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.” The Chinese government has dismissed the Times report as “groundless speculation.” China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips. Nvidia, a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models, is one of the world’s most valuable companies. Megaspeed was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the Times report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter. Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings about Huang’s relationship with the businesswoman roughly a year ago and chose not to act on the information, the Times report said. Trump said Sunday he did not regret not acting on this intelligence. “No, I don’t think so. I think — you know, he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. Y

item.title: Death Toll From Saudi Attack In Yemen Rises To 44
item.description: The death toll from Saudi strikes on Yemen’s Sanaa province climbed to 44, including more than 20 children, the Houthis said on their television channel Monday. A 2022 truce that had paused fighting in Yemen’s long-running conflict fell apart in July, restarting fighting between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government. Saudi Arabia has since traded blows with the Houthis, who have struck Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military sites. “The toll from the Saudi enemy’s massacre in the Alshariyah area of Bani Hushaysh, east of Sanaa, has risen to 84 casualties: 44 martyrs and 40 wounded,” the Houthis’ ministry of health said, according to the group’s Almasirah TV channel. Yemenis carry a body recovered from the rubble of a destroyed building after an airstrike reportedly carried out by Saudi Arabia on a village in the Bani Hushaysh district, located on the eastern outskirts of Sanaa on November 7, 2026. It said 21 children and 10 women were among those killed. “Rescue teams are still searching for the missing,” it added. The fresh toll comes after the Houthis claimed on Sunday an attack on the financial district of the Saudi capital Riyadh, with eyewitnesses saying they saw damage to a skyscraper belonging to oil giant Aramco. The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed in the impoverished country. item.title: Trump vows comeback as bitter showdown with Congress looms
item.description: Donald Trump vowed a political comeback Sunday as the major parties clashed over Democrat threats to prosecute top administration officials after the president’s Republicans lost control of Congress in midterm elections. The devastating results in last Tuesday’s vote leave Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure. It also opens the door to multiple investigations by the Democrat-controlled Congress of the president, his family and senior members of his administration. On political talk shows Sunday, incoming congressional leaders from the Democratic Party promised to hold Trump and his aides to account, while the president’s top law officer resolved to defend them and Trump dug in his heels on social media. “America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social, adding that the stock market that had grown during his tenure took a loss after the vote. “But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!” On Friday, a defiant Trump appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback — even though many Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, have reflected on why they had lost so badly at the ballot box. Miller was architect of Trump’s tough immigration policy, which analysts have identified as a contributing factor to the unpopularity of Republicans and their election debacle. Amid Democrat threats for administration officials to “lawyer up,” Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration, likening it to “extortion.” – Impeaching Hegseth? – With control of committees in both chambers of Congress, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny. Likely subjects include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Hakeem Jeffries, set to become speaker of the new Democrat-controlled House of Representatives, said he would support an effort to oust Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, a key architect of the war on Iran that began in February. “I’m a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution,” Jeffries told ABC, when asked about a Republican lawmaker’s reported plan to introduce an impeachment motion as early as Monday. “The so-called secretary of defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. item.title: SON uploads MANCAP-certified products online to check fakes
item.description: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria, SON, has uploaded the list of products certified under its Mandatory Conformity Assessment Programme, MANCAP, to its official website to enable consumers to identify and patronise quality Nigerian-made products. Director-General of SON, Dr Ifeanyi Okeke, disclosed this at the CANEX WKND 2026 held at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. Okeke, who was represented by the Director, Corporate Affairs Department, Mrs Talatu Ethan, said the initiative would enable consumers to verify certified products and make informed purchasing decisions. He said: “This development will help consumers find and buy quality products easily. It puts the power of choice in the hands of the Nigerian consumer, and it rewards manufacturers who have done the right thing by meeting our standards.” The SON boss urged members of the public to visit the organisation’s website to verify certified products, while encouraging them to report products bearing fake or questionable certification marks. He explained that SON’s participation at CANEX WKND 2026 was aimed at taking its quality assurance message directly to manufacturers, small business owners and consumers. “Our presence here is about meeting businesses where they are. Many creative and small enterprises have excellent products but do not know how to get them certified. Certification opens doors to bigger markets, here at home and across Africa, and it protects the consumer,” he said. At its exhibition stand, SON officials engaged exhibitors and visitors on product certification under the Nigerian Industrial Standards, NIS. They also educated participants on MANCAP, which covers locally manufactured products, and the SON Conformity Assessment Programme, SONCAP, applicable to imported products. Visitors were also sensitised on how to identify substandard and counterfeit products, verify the SON authentication mark and report suspicious goods. Small and medium-sized enterprises, SMEs, received guidance on the certification process, including application, product testing and eventual approval. Okeke stressed that locally manufactured products must meet international standards to compete effectively in global markets, particularly under the Federal Government’s Nigeria First policy. item.title: Nigerian woman entrepreneur wins award at World Investment Forum
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole A Nigerian woman entrepreneur, Biobele Oyibo, has won the Technology Award at the 2026 Empretec Women in Business Awards held during the 9th World Investment Forum in Doha, Qatar. Oyibo, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Earlybean, was recognised for leveraging technology to promote financial literacy and inclusion among young people. The awards organised under the theme, “Women-led businesses and the art of scale”, celebrated women entrepreneurs driving innovation, sustainability and business growth across four categories: Leadership, Sustainability, Innovation and Technology. The event brought together entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers and business leaders to celebrate the winners and connect them with funding, markets, expertise and networks to expand their businesses. The awards highlighted the role of women-led enterprises in creating jobs, deploying new technologies and addressing economic, social and environmental challenges. Other winners included Sandra Letio of Uganda, who received the Leadership Award for building an agribusiness that works with more than 5,000 smallholder farmers; and Paula Gianserra of Argentina, winner of the Sustainability Award for advancing forest restoration through artificial intelligence, biotechnology and drone seeding. The Innovation Award went to Aisha Albinali of Qatar, Co-Founder of Wafir, for transforming traditional savings practices into a financial technology solution, and Adriana Fernandes of Brazil, Chief Executive Officer of Mátrika Special Foods, for improving access to safe, quality food for people with allergies and dietary restrictions. As of Monday morning, November 9, 2026, the latest available official NFEM closing rate stood at approximately ₦1,346.79 per dollar, based on the November 6 market data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) In the parallel market, the dollar was quoted at approximately ₦1,415 to ₦1,430, depending on the dealer and location. This puts the gap between the official and parallel markets at about ₦68 to ₦83 per dollar. The parallel-market figures are indicative and may change throughout the day depending on dollar supply and demand. item.title: Flamingos Arrive In Abuja After FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup Victory
item.description: Victorious Flamingos landed in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Monday morning after their win at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup on Saturday. The team won their first FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup title after defeating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. The Flamingos became the first African team to win the competition, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. Officials of the Nigeria Football Federation and some supporters received the victorious Flamingos, who landed in the early hours of the day, at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja. The triumph is another landmark for a team that had already established itself as one of Africa’s leading sides at the age-grade level. Before travelling to Morocco, the Flamingos won the 2026 WAFU-B U-17 Girls Cup in Côte d’Ivoire, recording five victories from five matches, scoring 17 goals and conceding just once. ‘Victory Not A Fluke’ Flamingos head coach Hakeem Busari has praised his players for their resilience and tactical discipline after their impressive campaign at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, while expressing optimism about African football’s future. Busari, in a post-match interview, said the performance of African teams at the tournament reflected growing quality, character and competitiveness, despite the challenges posed by strong opposition. The Flamingos became the first African team to win the competition, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. He noted that the Flamingos had competed in a difficult group that included the defending champions, adding that the experience demonstrated the progress being made in African women’s youth football. “What we are seeing now is not a fluke. It is about development, it is about character, and it is about fighting from the beginning to really get it right. So we are elated and happy,” he said. The coach also expressed hope that more African teams would progress beyond the knockout stages in future editions of the competition and eventually reach the final. Reflecting on the Flamingos’ encounter with Japan, Busari explained that his technical crew had identified the Japanese team’s strength in winning second balls and exploiting spaces behind defensive lines. He said the team adjusted its approach to limit Japan’s attacking opportunities, particularly by directing long balls into spaces rather than areas where the opposition could easily gain possession. Busari explained that the Flamingos initially sought to score early before adopting a more cautious approach after taking the lead, but Japan eventually found an equaliser through a set-piece situation. He described the encounter as a tactical contest that required collective defending, discipline and effective game management. item.title: Manufacturers charged to deploy AI, energy-efficient technologies to cut costs
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) has urged manufacturers to embrace Artificial Intelligence (AI), advanced technologies and energy-efficient solutions to tackle rising production costs, strengthen energy security and improve industrial competitiveness. The call was made at the 2026 Manufacturers Energy Security and Energy Efficiency Summit in Lagos, where industry leaders and government representatives examined the role of technology, sustainable energy supply and structured financing in addressing the energy challenges confronting Nigerian manufacturers. The event was jointly organised by Manufacturers Power Development Company Ltd. (MPDCL), GIZ and the Nigerian Energy Support Programme (NESP). President of MAN, Ifeanyi Okoye, said the industrial energy cost reduction and adoption programme would promote factory rooftop solar installations, battery energy storage systems, captive natural gas solutions, and smart energy management networks. He said the programme was aimed at addressing the rising cost of energy, which had significantly affected manufacturing operations and competitiveness. According to him, manufacturers spend about 40 per cent of their profits addressing energy challenges, while high electricity tariffs, unreliable grid supply, and dependence on fossil fuels continued to undermine industrial production. “The summit is to facilitate access to long-term financing instruments, climate funds, green investments, and asset-financing mechanisms to support manufacturers’ transition to more efficient energy systems,” he said. In his comment, Director-General of MAN, Segun Ajayi-Kadir, said the adoption of emerging technologies had become critical to improving production efficiency, reducing energy consumption and strengthening the resilience of manufacturing operations. He noted that AI and smart manufacturing systems could help industries optimise energy use, minimise production losses, lower operating costs and improve product quality, particularly amid persistent electricity supply challenges. Chairman, Board of Directors, MPDCL, John Aluya, noted that the high cost of self-generation had reduced manufacturers’ profit margins and weakened their competitiveness. He stressed that reliable and affordable energy was critical to the survival of Nigerian industries, adding that the summit was meant to explore practical solutions, including solar photovoltaic systems, battery energy storage, captive gas power, energy efficiency, and carbon credit monetisation. In his keynote address, Ulf Brackmann, Chief Executive Officer of IKAPITAL Family Office & Friends, said AI could significantly boost industrial productivity and create new employment opportunities rather than displace workers, urging manufacturers to take advantage of the opportunities offered by technological innovation. Brackmann however noted that AI could only cut costs and boost efficiency for manufacturers where factories have dependable electrici

item.title: Power outages, rising costs slow manufacturing growth —NESG
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole Frequent power outages, rising production costs and limited access to credit are slowing manufacturing growth in Nigeria, with businesses struggling to sustain operations amid persistent infrastructure challenges, the October 2026 Business Confidence Monitor (BCM) by the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) has shown. The report indicated that manufacturing remained in expansion territory in October, but its Current Business Performance Index declined to 107.3 points from 108.4 points in September and 111.3 points in October 2025, reflecting a moderation in business activity. It identified incessant power outages, inadequate raw material supplies, high rental costs, limited access to credit and infrastructure deficiencies as major constraints confronting manufacturers during the month. According to NESG, these challenges continued to amplify operating costs, despite sustained expansion in business activities across the economy. The impact was particularly evident in key manufacturing subsectors. Textile, Apparel and Footwear slipped into contraction territory, with its performance index plunging to 99.7 points in October from 127.5 points in September. Cement also remained in contraction at 94.5 points, while Food, Beverage and Tobacco was the only one of the three major manufacturing subsectors to record improved performance and remain in expansion territory. The report’s findings underscore the growing burden of unreliable electricity on manufacturers, who depend on stable power supply to sustain production lines, process raw materials and maintain factory operations. Frequent outages force businesses to rely on alternative energy sources, adding to production costs and weakening their competitiveness. At the broader economy level, Nigeria’s Current Business Performance Index moderated to 115.4 points in October from 117.8 points in September, although it remained above the 111.3 points recorded in October 2025. All sectors remained in expansion territory, but only Trade and Services recorded improved performance compared with the preceding month. Agriculture, Manufacturing and Non-Manufacturing experienced slower growth. The cost pressures were also reflected in the NESG’s business indicators. The cost of doing business sub-index stood at 45.2 points in October, while the prices sub-index was 65.5 points, both significantly below the 100-point neutral threshold, indicating that most firms continued to face elevated operating costs and producer prices. Despite the challenges, the Future Business Expectations Index rose to 130.8 points in October from 128.9 points in September, signalling improved optimism about business conditions over the next one to three months. Manufacturing recorded an expectations index of 145.1 points, behind Trade at 194 points, but ahead of Non-Manufacturing at 135 points. item.title: ACAMB advises bank customers against phishing scams
item.description: The Association of Corporate Communication and Marketing Professionals in Banks (ACAMB) has urged bank customers to remain vigilant against phishing scams and other forms of cyber fraud, warning that criminals are increasingly using fake bank alerts, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal sensitive financial information. The warning follows a fraudulent text message impersonating various banks. FactCheckAfrica debunked the message, finding that the link it contained led to a cloned internet banking website designed to steal customers’ login credentials, BVNs, card details and transaction PINs. The incident highlights the risks associated with digital banking fraud in Nigeria. In June, Wema Bank suspended its engagements on X, (formerly known as Twitter) amid reports of more than 70 fake accounts impersonating the bank and its ALAT platform. In August, Zenith Bank Plc disclosed that it was investigating unauthorised access to customer data linked to a global cyberattack. ACAMB President, Jide Sipe, warned that fraudsters were increasingly adopting sophisticated methods to impersonate trusted banking brands and steal customers’ personal information, making their schemes difficult to distinguish from legitimate communications. “When a scam message carries your name, your phone number or your bank’s logo, it looks real. That is exactly why customers must slow down. No bank in Nigeria will ask you to confirm your PIN, password, OTP or BVN through a link,” Sipe said. Sipe acknowledged the efforts of banks to strengthen fraud detection and customer protection, alongside regulatory measures introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria’s mandatory cybersecurity self assessment guide. He stressed, however, that these efforts must be complemented by customer awareness and vigilance, particularly when handling requests for sensitive banking information. “Banks can strengthen their security systems, but fraudsters continue to find ways to exploit unsuspecting customers. We must all remain vigilant. Always pause, verify requests through official channels and report anything suspicious before taking action,” he added. Sipe urged customers to avoid clicking links in unsolicited messages asking them to verify, reactivate or secure their bank accounts. He also warned against sharing personal identification numbers (PINs), passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs), card verification values (CVVs) or BVNs in response to suspicious requests. Customers should verify such requests directly with their banks through official mobile applications, verified social media accounts or published customer service numbers.
