item.title: World Ports Confab: FG woos global investors with maritime reforms
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has intensified efforts to attract global investment into Nigeria’s maritime sector by showcasing the Federal Government’s ongoing port reforms and investor-friendly policies at the World Ports Conference, highlighting opportunities for private sector participation, improved port efficiency and sustainable growth. Speaking at the ongoing World Ports Conference in London, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, showcased President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s maritime policies and its positioning of Nigeria’s Ports as Africa’s biggest economy that is yearning for global investment. He affirmed that the speed of growth and development in the country’s ports signifies the huge opportunities investors should tap into, adding that the current administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has put policies in place that are investment friendly. The NPA boss identified Nigeria’s huge population, urbanization, and infrastructural gaps in the ports as attractive opportunities for investment in its maritime and associated sectors. Dantsoho, who is also the Vice- President of the International Association of Ports & Harbours (IAPH) and doubles as Chairman of the Port Management Association of West and Central Africa (PMAWCA) told investors that Africa’s untapped resources remain the best destination for ports investment and development. He said the government alone cannot fund development of bigger or deeper sea ports and other similar projects hence the need for investors to take advantage of such opportunities across the continent. Dantsoho affirmed that “Nigeria has the highest population in Africa. So, the speed of growth is something that really should concern us. For example, in Nigeria, only recently, about 3 years ago, we commissioned the first deep sea port in Nigeria, which is called Lekki Deep Sea Port, that was funded by the Chinese government in relationship with China Harbor, and the expenditure cost us $1.6 billion to build Lekki in Lagos. item.title: BoI advocates investment in industrial clusters to boost Lagos economy
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Bank of Industry (BOI) has called for increased investment in industrial clusters, reliable power supply and supporting infrastructure to boost productivity, attract private capital and strengthen the Lagos State economy. Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, BoI, Dr. Olasupo Olusi made this call in a keynote address delivered at the 4th edition of the Lagos Economic Outlook 2027 Discourse, themed, ‘“Development Pathways, Emerging Risks and Strategic Policy Priorities.’ Represented by Dr. Isa Omagu, General Manager, MD/CEO’s Office, BoI, Olusi said investment in industrial clusters, particularly along major industrial and port corridors, would help businesses overcome production constraints, reduce operating costs and improve their competitiveness. He also said Lagos must assess economic progress by the improvements businesses and residents experience, rather than relying solely on economic growth figures and public spending. “The test is whether Lagos becomes more productive and more liveable,” he said. He identified electricity costs, traffic congestion, access to appropriate financing and institutional coordination as major constraints to business productivity. “A manufacturer needs reliable electricity. A worker needs a commute that does not consume productive hours. Firms need predictable approvals, appropriate finance and customers,” he said. Olusi urged the state to prioritise investment in power infrastructure serving industrial clusters, faster freight movement, streamlined business approvals, flood-resilient commercial routes and skills development. Speaking at the event, Lagos State Commissioner for Economic Planning and Budget, Mr. Ope George, said the ministry would continue to coordinate economic intelligence, development planning, budget management and performance monitoring in support of Lagos State’s long-term development aspirations. He said the 2027 economic outlook provided an opportunity to consolidate the state’s achievements, address structural challenges and strengthen its position as a competitive and resilient economy. “Our focus goes beyond economic projections. It is about shaping policies that will strengthen competitiveness, promote inclusive growth and secure a sustainable future for Lagos State,” George said. Earlier, Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Economic Planning and Budget, Mrs. Olayinka Ojo, highlighted the state’s development planning, budget monitoring and performance evaluation frameworks. She said Lagos was strengthening evidence-based governance through its long-term development plan, Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, annual budgets and regular monitoring of revenue, expenditure and project delivery. Ojo also highlighted the government’s engagement with communities and the use of platforms to improve citizens’ access to information on public projects and social intervention programmes. item.title: Customs frees 98 containers of power equipment stranded for 20 years
item.description: •Cargoes to ease pressure on substations, strengthen national grid — Tegbe By Udeme Akpan The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has released 98 containers of electricity transmission equipment stranded at the nation’s ports, some for up to 20 years, in a move expected to strengthen the national grid and improve electricity supply across the country. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this in Lagos, stating that 44 containers were released from ENL Terminal, while another 54 were cleared from APMT and Sun & Moon Terminals. He said the 98 containers represented part of more than 300 containers of transmission equipment held at the ports. The equipment, comprising high-capacity transformers, cables and switchgear, was procured to expand the transmission network, address overloaded substations and improve electricity delivery nationwide. Tegbe said: “The equipment was procured to expand the transmission network and relieve overloaded substations. Its detention stalled projects, kept existing substations under heavy strain, exposed valuable assets to deterioration and accumulated charges on the cargoes.” He noted that the prolonged detention of the equipment had imposed additional costs on businesses, households and public institutions, which continued to grapple with unreliable electricity supply. Also speaking, the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adeniyi, said the Service had commenced processes to clear the containers in collaboration with the Ministry of Power, the Nigerian Ports Authority and terminal operators. He said: “The release follows the President’s directive for immediate clearance and for agencies to resolve outstanding charges and administrative bottlenecks without delay.” Adeniyi pledged to work with the Minister until all the containers were cleared, while appealing to terminal operators to support the national effort. The Minister disclosed that an inspection of the recovered equipment showed that most of the items remained useful and viable. He said: “When evacuated, it will be verified, tested and refurbished where necessary, then deployed to project sites to complete stalled installations, relieve overloaded substations and strengthen constrained transmission corridors.” The post Customs frees 98 containers of power equipment stranded for 20 years appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: COP31 Opens As Climate, Geopolitical Pressures Mount
item.description: The UN’s annual climate talks kick off Monday in Turkey as rising temperatures heighten the urgency of action, with financial constraints and geopolitical tensions complicating efforts to secure global cooperation. More than 100,000 people are expected to attend COP31 in a sprawling expo centre in the Mediterranean seaside city of Antalya over the next two weeks. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are facing tough discussions over how to accelerate the energy transition and provide funds to help developing nations cope with the worsening climate emergency. But observers say few major breakthroughs are expected as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. The climate emergency, meanwhile, continued to wreak havoc this year as punishing heatwaves baked Europe, wildfires raged in Indonesia, and a glacier collapse triggered devastating floods in Nepal. An exceptionally strong El Niño climate phenomenon is forecast to peak later this year, adding to extreme weather and possibly helping to make 2026 or 2027 the hottest year on record. The outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above preindustrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement. “Global leaders must pull us back from the brink and commit to rapidly transitioning away from fossil fuels and expanding renewable energy, an imperative reinforced by the current energy affordability crisis,” said Rachel Cleetus, climate programme director at the Union of Concerned Scientists. A woman walks inside the COP31 venue at the Antalya Expo Center on November 8, 2026, ahead of the opening of the UN climate conference. ‘Clean’ Electrification? Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference. The partners have branded the summit as the “implementation COP”, focusing on turning commitments into concrete action after years of pledges and ambitious announcements. Turkey is promoting an “action agenda” alongside the formal negotiations that encourages countries to support non-binding pledges on issues from artificial intelligence to waste management. Its centrepiece is an “electrification” drive to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20 percent today to 35 percent by 2035. But the initiative could become a source of friction. The European Union has called for “clean” electrification, a term that could spark debate over the role of fossil fuels in the Turkish proposal. Countries committed to transition away from fossil fuels in a landmark pact at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 but have struggled to agree on how to turn that pledge into action. item.title: British people don’t trust Palantir – it’s not too late to reverse the NHS’s dependence on it | Ben Coleman
item.description: We can’t allow our health data to be locked into the control of a US tech firm. It won’t be easy, but next spring the job of clawing it back must begin Ben Coleman is Labour MP for Chelsea and Fulham and a member of the health and social care committee Next March, Palantir’s £330m contract to run NHS England’s federated data platform (FDP) ends. Ministers must decide by Christmas whether to extend it. They should move on from Palantir, and transition to new suppliers that put the NHS in full control of its technology and patient data. I sit on the health and social care committee. In June, we recommended no extension – people don’t trust Palantir , its benefits are contested and other tools could deliver the same or similar advantages. The debate so far has been whether to drop Palantir. The harder question is what replaces it. The tempting solution is to hire a single British firm. But that would not give the NHS the control it lacks: the freedom to switch supplier without losing what it has built. item.title: Comedian Russell Brand To Be Sentenced For Rape, Assaults
item.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand, who became a household name in the 2000s as a sex-obsessed provocateur, will find out on Monday how long he will spend in jail, after he was convicted of rape and sexual assaults. Brand’s conviction last week marked the final blow in a scandal-hit showbiz career that saw him embody the anything-goes culture of 2000s British TV and radio. On Monday, he will be sentenced at London’s Southwark Crown Court, where he was told by the judge he faced a “significant custodial term” after being found guilty of one rape and three sexual assaults against four women, committed between 2004 and 2009. The maximum sentence in the UK for rape is life imprisonment. Brand, 51, who was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault, was remanded in custody and spent the weekend in a cell. He is facing further investigations after London’s Metropolitan Police said it was probing rape allegations by two more women. (FILES) British actor and comedian Russell Brand addresses an anti-austerity rally in Parliament Square in London on June 21, 2014. London’s Metropolitan Police on Friday said it had charged comedian and actor Russell Brand with rape and a number of other sexual offences. (Photo by Justin TALLIS / AFP) From Channel 4 to MTV and an eponymous primetime show on BBC Radio 2, the wild-haired comedian passed through major British media houses in the 2000s, where his obsession with sex contributed to his notoriety. That behaviour was also a feature of the high-profile trial, with Brand admitting that he had been “extremely promiscuous” and had used his fame to “facilitate sexual access”, although he denied the charges. He was accompanied to court most days by his wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children. Calling him a “wonderful father to our children”, Gallacher told the jury that when they first dated in 2006: “It was clear it was difficult for him to be monogamous.” She said she was “very aware” of Brand’s promiscuity, as “you could read about it regularly in the papers”. British comedian and actor Russell Brand (C) leaves following a hearing at Southwark Crown Court in south London on May 30, 2025. Brand pleaded not guilty to five charges of rape and sexual assault. (Photo by HENRY NICHOLLS / AFP) ‘Shapeshifter’ Brand’s hypersexualised persona was a running joke in tabloids, with the comedian named “shagger of the year” three years in a row by The Sun newspaper from 2006-2009. “He’s a bit of a shapeshifter,” then-showbiz editor of The Sun, Gordon Smart told Channel 4. “He would present to you as he thought appropriate, quite chameleon-like.” Born to working-class parents in Essex, east of London in 1975, Brand dropped out of drama school before joining MTV at the age of 25. He was fired for turning up to work dressed as Osama bin Laden following the 9/11 terror attacks and for inviting his drug dealer into the studios. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 9 – Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 9 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula Explanation: Does the blue nebula look like the head of a witch? The nebula is known popularly as the Witch Head Nebula because, it is said, the nebula’s shape resembles a Halloween-style caricature of a witch’s head. Exactly how, though, can be a topic of imaginative speculation . What is clear is that IC 2118 is about 50 light-years across and made of gas and dust that points to — because it has been partly eroded by — the nearby star Rigel . One of the brighter stars in the constellation Orion, Rigel lies just below the center of the featured image . The blue color of the Witch Head Nebula and is caused not only by Rigel’s intense blue starlight but also because the dust grains scatter blue light more efficiently than red. The same physical process causes Earth’s daytime sky to appear blue , although the scatterers in planet Earth’s atmosphere are molecules of nitrogen and oxygen . item.description: The writer and podcaster on why politics is made to seem more complicated than it is and his mission to unpack world events for everyone Why did you get into comedy? My mum was a professional dancer and always encouraged me to perform. Given that I have zero rhythm, comedy was my other option. She wrote me a poem called Mrs Brown’s Moggy, about a cat that was often very soggy, for my school’s talent show. Because you can’t tell the difference between real and polite laughter at the age of six, I assumed I’d killed my first gig and convinced myself I was born to do nothing else. Where do you find your material? In a world where Robert Jenrick claims Nigel Farage has “ probably done more than almost anybody to stand against racism ”, the answer is that my material is presented to me on a silver platter each morning. item.title: Ozone Hole Reaches Its 2026 Maximum
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Ozone Hole Reaches Its 2026… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search This data visualization shows the area and shape of the ozone hole on September 18, 2026, the day of its annual maximum extent. Scientists define the ozone hole as the area in which ozone concentrations drop below the historical threshold of 220 Dobson units. NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin This story is an update to the Antarctic ozone hole feature in our World of Change series , which documents how Earth changes over months, seasons, and years. The stratospheric ozone layer protects life on Earth by absorbing ultraviolet light, which damages DNA in plants and animals (including humans) and leads to sunburns and skin cancer. Prior to 1979, scientists had not observed atmospheric ozone concentrations below 220 Dobson Units . But in 1985, British Antarctic Survey scientists using ground-based measurements at Halley Research Station reported that Earth’s natural sunscreen was thinning dramatically over Antarctica each spring. NASA satellite instruments revealed the continental scale of this Antarctic ozone thinning, and it came to be known as the ozone hole. The data visualizations below shows the ozone hole each year from 1979 through 2026 (no data are available for 1995). The measurements were made from 1979-2004 by the TOMS (NASA’s Total Ozone Mapping Spectrometer) instruments on Nimbus-7 and several additional satellites; from 2005-2011 by the OMI (Ozone Monitoring Instrument) on the Aura satellite; from 2012-2025 by the OMPS (Ozone Mapping and Profiler Suite) on the Suomi NPP satellite; and in 2026 by the OMPS on the NOAA-20 satellite. Red and yellow areas indicate the ozone hole. As the images show, the word hole isn’t literal; no place is empty of ozone. Scientists use the word hole as a metaphor for the area in which ozone concentrations drop below the historical threshold of 220 Dobson Units . Using this metaphor, they can describe the hole’s area and depth. These maps show the state of the ozone hole each year on the day of maximum depth—the day the lowest ozone concentrations were measured. 1979 1980 1981 1982 1983 1984 1985 1986 1987 1988 1989 1990 1991 1992 1993 1994 1996 1997 1998 1999 2000 2001 2002 2003 2004 2005 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 2015 2016 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 2026 The series begins in 1979. The maximum depth of the hole that year was 194 Dobson Units (DU)—not far below the previous historical low. For several years, the maximum depth stayed in the 190s, but then rapidly grew deeper: 173 DU in 1982, 154 in 1983, 124 in 1985. By

item.title: Linus Torvalds sees signs AI-prompted patch flood has peaked
item.description: The worst of the patchpocalypse may be behind us, according to Linus Torvalds. Writing in his weekly kernel update post , the Linux kernel dev leader delivered Linux 7.4 rc2 – the second rough cut of the next kernel – which he rated as a big release for two reasons. One is that he left some code out of rc1, because he was busy and because it was already the largest such release in the history of the kernel. The other is what Torvalds described as “various AI fixes.” Such fixes are necessary because ever since Anthropic launched its Mythos bug-finding model in April , developers have been able to find more software flaws than was previously possible. Microsoft, for example, addressed a record 974 flaws in September – its third record fixing spree this year after it whacked 622 flaws in July and 206 in June. Oracle addressed 1,449 flaws in a single month. That’s many more patches than IT teams are set up to handle, yet they must find ways to deal with bugs more quickly because attackers are increasingly targeting flaws found by AI . Torvalds’ post suggests that, perhaps, the worst of this is behind us. “This time around Alexei claims that on the bpf side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true,” he wrote. That’s a reference to Alexei Starovoitov, co-creator and lead dev on the Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF), the project that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs within the Linux kernel. “I think most other areas haven't reached that point yet, but it's at least a sign that we _may_ be starting to see the tide starting to turn,” he added. “Don't hold your breath, but maybe cross your fingers we'll be getting there in the not entirely distant future.” If Torvalds is correct, that’s welcome news. The Linux kernel’s 40-million-plus lines of code makes it one of the world’s bigger software projects. If AI soon stops finding flaws in other parts of the kernel beyond eBPF, perhaps the deluge of fixes developers and users alike will need to handle has peaked. ®

item.title: Bandits burn 12 family members
item.description: Twelve members of the same family have been killed after armed bandits set their residence ablaze during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. Seven other residents were also abducted during the attack, which occurred on Saturday night in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward, despite efforts by the community to alert security agencies. This is coming barely one week after bandits ambushed security personnel at Gidan Kano along the Gusau-Sokoto highway within the same local government and killed five policemen. A resident, who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, said the attackers invaded the residence of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani at about 10 pm. 1 killed in NDC rally as attacks rise Middle Belt leaders’ visit to Tinubu raises unity questions He said 13 members of the family were trapped inside a room after locking themselves in to escape being abducted by the attackers. According to him, those inside the room included Sani, his two wives and their six children, as well as the wife of his younger brother and their three children. He said the bandits ordered the occupants to open the door, but when they refused, the attackers set the room ablaze. Only the wife of Sani’s younger brother reportedly escaped, while the remaining 12 occupants died from the intense heat and fire. The resident said the community immediately contacted the Maradun Local Government Chairman, Sanusi Ahmed Dosara, who made efforts to reach security formations for assistance. However, he said the security agencies could not intervene before the tragedy occurred. “We informed the local government chairman, Dosara, and he tried all he could to reach the security personnel. He told us he had spoken with different security formations, but nobody came to our rescue,” he said. He expressed disappointment that no security personnel responded to their distress calls despite the village’s proximity to Maradun town, where military and police formations are located. “Imagine, the distance between our village and Dosara is just about half a kilometre, while from Dosara to Maradun is about one kilometre. In total, it is just about one and a half kilometres between our village and the local government headquarters. “There is a military base in Maradun, a mobile police base and a police headquarters, yet none of them came to our aid until the bandits burnt the 12 people alive,” he said. Another resident confirmed that seven other people were abducted during the attack and remained in the custody of the bandits as of the time he spoke to Daily Trust. He appealed to security agencies to strengthen their presence in the area and take urgent measures to protect residents against further attacks. He also disputed reports of police reinforcement in the village, saying officers only visited to obtain information about the incident and left. “The police only came to make inquiries, just the way you are doing now as a journalist. item.title: Huawei says it’s made a 100 percent Chinese PC
item.description: Huawei claims it’s built a desktop PC that uses only parts made in CHina. The company launched the Qingyun HM650 last week and said it uses Huawei’s own Kirin X90 processor, a ten-core 20-thread machine with a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The machine runs a newly developed enterprise version of HarmonyOS, the OS Huawei developed to end its dependence on Android and which it intends to run on most of the devices it makes. A single Chinese government agency has reportedly signed up for 600 of the machines. That’s not an indication this machine is a curiosity, because Beijing has ordered all government entities to shift from Wintel boxes to local alternatives. While Huawei has reportedly claimed local companies manufactured 100 percent of the components in the machine, it is unclear if all those components use Chinese designs. The Register mentions that uncertainty as many non-Chinese companies continue to operate factories in China. Even if Huawei is using some parts that aren’t entirely Chinese, the debut of the Qingyun HM650 is bad news for Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm, as all are suffering as the PC market shrinks due to the rising cost of memory. China’s government is an enormous buyer, and losing the chance to bid for its business is unlikely to be helpful. The ¥10 billion ($63 million) package follows a wave of cyberattacks that have disrupted railways, retailers, KFC’s logistics provider , and cloud computing operators . The emergency package aims to help Japanese government agencies to use AI to nail infosec basics, and to build tools that let the National Cybersecurity Office aggregate information about cyberattacks. Some funds will also go towards supporting victims. item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang starring in possible remake of The Spy Who Shagged Me
item.description: Nvidia’s board has opened an investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a romantic relationship with a woman US authorities feel is likely a Chinese spy. The AI hardware giant’s board published a statement on Sunday afternoon that states it is “initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The New York Times is the source of that reporting . On October 29 it alleged US government intelligence agencies decided to investigate a woman who goes by Alice Huang and/or Huang Le, on grounds she passes intelligence with Beijing. In that story The Times used the term “close relationship” to describe the Nvidia CEO's associations with both Ms Huang and US president Donald Trump. On Sunday the newspaper alleged US authorities believe Alice Huang and Jensen Huang shared a "romantic" relationship. The Times further alleges Ms Huang is a Chinese citizen who worked for a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed that has bought plenty of Nvidia hardware and is suspected of doing so to make it available to Chinese users, either by running inside datacenters or perhaps even facilitating transport to the Middle Kingdom. The US has for years banned or restricted exports of advanced GPUs to China, partly because it feels Beijing’s armed forces can use them to build systems that will erode America’s military superiority. Any relationship, of any sort, between Jensen Huang and a Chinese intelligence operative would therefore be enormously concerning. The company told the NYT that Jensen Huang and Alice Huang just had normal CEO-to-customer-exec chats that were no threat to Nvidia intellectual property or US national security. Shortly after Nvidia’s board published its statement, Huang sent an email to staff that the company made public . “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” the email opens. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang’s email doesn’t explicitly link his actions to The Times’ reports, but he says he supports the Nvidia board’s decision to open its investigation “and will cooperate fully.” "To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me," he wrote, without specifying if that's a reference to infidelity. "Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence." “I love our country and our company,” the CEO added. “I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.” The CEO’s mail, and the board’s statement, make no allegations about any “close r

item.title: Apple’s M5 MacBook Air is down to its lowest price since July
item.description: A top-down view of the 15-inch MacBook Air, which features Apple’s M5 processor. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge The latest 13-inch MacBook Air is currently available for $1,099.99, marking the second time we’ve seen this $200 discount following the company’s hefty price increases over the summer . Although the base model — which features Apple’s M5 processor, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage — often sold for around $950 to $1,000 shortly after it launched in May, savings have been rare since July, making the current deal worth flagging. Amazon , Best Buy , and B&H Photo are all honoring the price across all color options. If you’d prefer something with a larger screen, a six-speaker array instead of four, and slightly more power (with two additional GPU cores in the M5), Apple’s 15-inch MacBook Air is also on sale for $200 off. Amazon , Best Buy , and B&H Photo are each selling the 16GB RAM / 512GB SSD configuration in most colors for $1,299.99. Apple 13-inch MacBook Air (M5) Where to Buy: $1299 $1099 at Amazon $1299 $1099 at Best Buy $1299 $1099 at B&H Photo Although it’s pricier than the newer MacBook Neo, the Air offers better value in numerous ways. It’s an ideal choice if you want faster performance, as it offers double the RAM and a speedier CPU with more cores. You also get twice as much storage, better speakers, a backlit keyboard, and a larger, higher-resolution screen. Given said differences, it’s easy to see how the Air’s improvements might make it worth the extra cost for some people. If you’re still on the fence, though, I’d recommend reading my colleague Antonio G. Di Benedetto’s reviews, both of which were published before the summer price increases. Read our full MacBook Neo and M5 MacBook Air reviews.

item.title: Legendary sci-fi magazine 'Starlog' returns as a yearly release, just in time for its 50th anniversary
item.description: null "Starlog" was one of the greatest sci-fi and fantasy magazines ever, and after a 17-year absence, it's being resurrected. The legendary sci-fi mag went dark back in 2009 as part of the wave of popular publications folding due to years of declining readership and subscriptions. But as of Nov. 13, this geek favorite periodical returns as an annual print edition, and it's available for pre-order now. It’s another indication of digital fatigue in the world, and fans of a certain age will recall the pleasure of poring over each colorful issue packed with in-depth interviews, behind-the-scenes photos, TV guides, classic movie retrospectives, book reviews, con news, and VFX features. The triumphant relaunch of "Starlog" magazine happens on Nov. 13, 2026 (Image credit: Fangoria Holdings) "Starlog" launched in 1976, in the pre-" Star Wars " days, under the leadership of editor-in-chief Kerry O’Quinn. It first arrived with artist Jack Thurston's beautiful painted "Star Trek" cover, featuring William Shatner as Captain James T. Kirk and Leonard Nimoy’s Spock, set against the U.S.S. Enterprise near a shimmering black hole. The magazine continued to inform the science fiction community about upcoming sci-fi TV shows and blockbuster Hollywood films for over three decades; I fondly recall reading each informative and entertaining monthly issue cover-to-cover. Just in time to honor its 50th anniversary this year, "Starlog" blasts back into the sci-fi universe with Issue #375 showcasing cover artwork created by Armenian artist Gabriel Yeganyan. Its geek culture legacy, covering iconic franchises like "Star Wars," "Star Trek," and "Alien," will now live on thanks to Fangoria Holdings and io9 co-founder Annalee Newitz, editor-in-chief. Three vintage "Starlog" magazine issues from my personal collection! (Image credit: Jeff Spry) "During its original 33-year run, 'Starlog' documented science fiction as it evolved across film, television, books, technology, and culture," said 'Fangoria's Tara Ansley. "Fifty years after the magazine first launched, the line between science fiction and the real world has become increasingly difficult to separate. That makes this an especially interesting time to bring 'Starlog' back. Technology may change, but the most compelling questions have always been about people: how we live, what we create, and what kind of future we want to build." "Starlog" reloads for its first annual edition after a long hiatus on Nov. 13. You can pre-order the first issue (Issue 375 in continuity) on the Starlog website .

item.title: NASA Announces $1 Million to Students for Moon Base Challenge
item.description: Artist’s concept depicting astronauts, habitats, rovers, power systems, and cargo operations supporting sustained human activities at the Moon Base near the lunar South Pole. Credit: NASA On Sunday, NASA announced the opening of its $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge during a MAX POWER event at Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Florida. As part of a Golden Age of Science, the competition invites student teams at U.S. high schools and post-secondary schools to contribute designs for the Moon Base. “We’re looking for students ready to think creatively, work as a team, and take on real problems connected to NASA’s future on the Moon,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “You do not have to wait until graduation to contribute. Curiosity, creativity, and the willingness to tackle hard problems without obvious answers are exactly the qualities we need as we build what comes next.” NASA is building a Moon Base where astronauts will live, work, and explore at the lunar South Pole region. A permanent human presence on the Moon paves the way for future crewed missions to Mars and requires talent from various industries and backgrounds. “As we build and design the foundations of Moon Base, we want to leverage all the ingenuity and innovation to think of every consideration our explorers might need to live and work there,” said Carlos García-Galán, manager, Moon Base Program. “Students bring exactly the bold ideas that we’re looking for, and I’m looking forward to their fresh perspective. Ultimately, Moon Base is for them, people who will experience a world where humans are on the Moon to stay.” The multiphase challenge supports NASA’s commitment to cultivating the technical skills of tomorrow’s aerospace workforce. For this challenge, student teams will design innovative solutions for Moon Base across six categories: power generation and storage, construction, life-support systems, surface mobility, communications networks, and astronaut safety. The challenge gives participants an opportunity to develop necessary skills for careers in the space industry while helping advance new concepts for Moon Base technologies. Participants are required to register for the challenge through the NASA STEM Gateway. Registration is open until Jan. 25, 2027. “Students are the next generation of explorers and innovators. Their unique perspectives are key to helping us envision a future away from Earth, and I’m excited to see the creativity and ingenuity spurred by this challenge,” said Elaine Ho, associate administrator for the Office of STEM Engagement at NASA Headquarters. The Moon Base Student Challenge addresses authentic environmental and mission design parameters for life and operations on the lunar surface. The deliverables reflect industry skills – such as trade studies, concept proposals, and stakeholder briefings – allowing participants across technical, vocational, and various academic tracks to build career-relevant skills without requiring prior sp

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
item.description: null On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this. It performed well, but eventually it stopped listening to commands. The spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere in January 2015. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the Venus Express spacecraft to Venus on Nov. 8, 2005.. (Image credit: ESA) Why it mattered Venus Express established ESA as the third world organization to successfully send a probe to study Venus, following the United States and Soviet Union. (Japan's JAXA became the fourth five years later.) "By studying Venus, scientists learn how Earth-like planets change over time," reads a summary of the planet's exploration prepared by The Planetary Society. "Orbital studies [like Venus Express] hint that Venus may have hosted habitable oceans before becoming inhospitable." "By studying Venus, we can learn how Earth-like planets evolve and what shapes planets throughout the galaxy into temperate, lush worlds instead of sweltering hothouses. Venus also helps scientists model Earth’s climate, and may serve as a cautionary tale on how dramatically a planet’s climate can change," wrote the Society. An illustration of the Venus Express spacecraft in orbit around Venus. (Image credit: ESA) ESA returned to Venus in 2018 when BepiColombo, its joint mission with JAXA, used the planet's gravity to redirect its path toward the planet Mercury. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Who is King Ghidorah? The cosmic connections of Godzilla Minus Zero's foe
item.description: null Godzilla goes toe-to-toe with long-time foe King Ghidorah in Godzilla Minus Zero, which opened in theaters on Friday (Nov. 6). Though the three-headed golden Kaiju might seem like a natural native of Monster Island, King Ghidorah actually emerged from the depths of space. However, it isn't just the origins of King Ghidorah — also known as Monster Zero in the Godzilla movie Invasion of Astro-Monster (1965) — that are this beast's only cosmic connection. One of the largest structures in the universe, the King Ghidorah Supercluster , was named in honor of Godzilla's primary antagonist. Eat that, King Kong! King Ghidorah and Godzilla The three heads of King Ghidorah seen in Godzilla Minus Zero (Image credit: Toho Studios) King Ghidorah is a three-headed, twin-tailed golden dragon from the stars, first introduced in the fifth Godzilla movie, Ghidorah, the Three-Headed Monster (1964). In this first appearance, part of the Shōwa era (1964–1975) of Godzilla history, Ghidorah ravaged Venus , wiping out its population 5,000 years before arriving on Earth encased within a highly magnetic meteorite . Ghidorah was bested this first time by Godzilla, Rodan, and Mothra. Undeterred, Ghidorah returned for a rematch just a year later in Invasion of Astro Monster (1965), after being discovered supposedly terrorizing the inhabitants of Planet X, a world found beyond Jupiter . In this movie, it is revealed that Ghidorah is less a king and more a pawn, under the control of calculating Xiliens as part of a plan to subjugate Earth. This will become a theme. King Ghidorah flying and blasting lightning from its three mouths in Invasion of Astro Monster (1965). (Image credit: Toho Studios) Freed from that control, Ghidorah returns to deep space, once again falling under the thrall of an alien race in 1968's Destroy All Monsters. This movie sees Ghidorah hold its own against a who's who of kaiju, eventually succumbing to the combined might of Godzilla, Minilla, Mothra, Rodan, Manda, Gorosaurus, Anguirus, Kumonga, Baragon, and Varan. Even with three gravity-beam-blasting heads, that is hardly fair! Ghidorah returned with some backup for a final time in the Shōwa era in 1975's Godzilla vs. Gigan. This time, Ghidorah and his tag-team partner Gigan (who resembled a giant one-eyed space chicken) were under the control of cockroach-like Nebulans. Getting mind-controlled three times is just embarrassing! Fortunately, the Shōwa era drew to a close in 1975 before Ghidorah was forced into servitude for a fourth time. Mecha-King Ghidorah battling Godzilla in Godzilla Vs. King Ghidorah (1991). (Image credit: Tohu Pictures) Ghidorah returned in the rebooted Godzilla timeline of the Heisei era (1991–1998) in 1991's Godzilla Vs. King Ghidorah, but its cosmic origins are gone. The Heisei Ghidorah begins life as three genetically engineered creatures called Dorats in the future before being morphed into a three-headed form via nuclear exposure. item.title: Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
item.description: Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don't agree on why. In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate. The missing electrons Central to the mystery of cuprates’ high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. “The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons,” Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be. “Everybody knows that from different probes, you see that there's these vanishing electrons, but nobody knows why,” Allan said. Read full article Comments

Yet, in England, about 95% of adult hospital beds were occupied at the height of flu season last year. item.title: Doom delivers five minutes of terminal violence on an IBM mainframe
item.description: Can an IBM Z mainframe run Doom? Of course it can. The more interesting question is whether you can play it through a text terminal without ruining your eyesight. WND Software's browser demo connects to an IBM Z mainframe over SSH using its terminal emulator. Wojciech Graj's DOOM-ASCII supplies the text-based carnage, replacing conventional graphics with colored characters. There's no sound. It is, however, completely playable (although you might need to recalibrate your vision to work out what is going on, particularly with regard to distant objects). Sessions are limited to five minutes, with room for up to 50 simultaneous users, but we had no trouble getting in. ASCII also presented no issues once the game was in motion. This writer played the original shareware release on an Amstrad ALT386SX portable, so squinting at an indistinct demon felt reassuringly familiar. That Doom can be persuaded to run on an IBM Z mainframe is not particularly noteworthy. The code has turned up everywhere from databases to PCB designers . Even the humble Pi Pico was roped into the fun. Keeping the action playable through a text terminal is the more entertaining achievement. A year ago, an IBM consultant persuaded Doom to run on IBM Z and LinuxONE using VNC to bring the pixelated mayhem to life. Using a terminal emulator, while a neat demonstration of the capabilities of WND's software, is perhaps more an example of "because I can" masochism. It's undeniably an enjoyable way to burn through five minutes. No installation or login required – just a willingness to shoot at punctuation. ®

item.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
item.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. An illustration shows the landscape of a primordial Earth before life arose as lightning splits the skies (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) What makes the simulation especially useful is its plug-and-play nature. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. If the result is a planet with an atmosphere that matches what is detected spectroscopically by the James Webb Space Telescope or, in the future, the various extremely large 30-meter-plus ground-based telescopes or NASA’s planned Habitable Worlds Observatory , then we know that planet probably does not have life as we know it. However, if the simulated planet without life does not match what we observe on the real planet, then it becomes possible that life is present and altering the atmosph

item.title: Internet governance about to get its quadrennial stress test at ITU meeting
item.description: The International Telecommunications Union (ITU) kicks off its quadrennial plenipotentiary on Monday, and internet governance organizations are bracing in case the event becomes a forum for nation-states to try to challenge their roles. The ITU is the United Nations' specialized agency for information and communication technologies, meaning its members are nation-states. The body's role is to facilitate international connectivity, which it does by managing radio spectrum, satellite orbits, and working on relevant technical standards. Its key standards are pervasive. ITU-T X.509 sets out the rules of public key infrastructure. ITU-T E.164 governs telephone numbers. ITU-T H.264 and 265 define the video codecs used for most online streams. The ITU's role is largely uncontested, yet its work gets very close to that of the organizations who work on technologies that make the internet work. Those bodies include the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF); the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), which oversees the domain name system; and the regional internet registries (RIRs), which manage IP addresses. The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) works on HTML, CSS, and accessibility. Governments participate in work at those internet governance bodies but are just one voice among many and can't override the consensus-driven decision-making process they use, under a system which has come to be known as the multi-stakeholder governance model. At a 2025 event called WSIS+20, the United Nations endorsed multi-stakeholder governance by deciding that its Internet Governance Forum (IGF) should become a permanent body. That decision effectively endorsed multi-stakeholder governance, and kept the ITU out of internet standards. Yet the IGF hasn't met since WSIS+20, so it is yet to start operating meaningfully as a permanent body. This year's ITU meeting is therefore a moment at which stakeholders can stress-test the delicate balance between the ITU, internet governance bodies, and the emerging IGF. Such a test could see ITU members try to have it pursue new fields that overlap with work performed by internet governance organizations. This has already happened before. China tried to have the ITU work on " New IP" – a major revision to internet protocol, a technology the IETF manages. In 2022, Russia and China backed a candidate for the ITU presidency who favored giving nations a stronger role in internet governance, potentially by having the ITU take over some standards work. That candidate was not elected. Ahead of next week's meetings, the Internet Society published a background paper that declared it is "actively challenging proposals that could affect the Internet's underlying technical architecture or increase fragmentation, as well as those that could affect connectivity, particularly for remote, underserved, and unserved communities." The society is watching for resolutions on AI, quantum technologies, and other emerging areas that could em

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 8 – Major Fireball Meteor
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 8 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Major Fireball Meteor Explanation: The sky glows with soft pinkish colors of fading twilight in this serendipitous mountaintop vista. Taken in subfreezing temperatures, the thoughtfully composed photo shows snowy, rugged peaks seen from a mountain pass on 2017 November 14. Below lies the village of La Villa, Alta Badia in Italy ‘s Dolomite Alps . Above the nestled village lights, the constellation Ursa Major hangs over the northern horizon. But most stunning is the intense fireball meteor. It was captured during the camera’s exposure by chance as it flashed east to west across the northern horizon, under Ursa Major’s familiar Big Dipper asterism . Sightings of this major fireball meteor were widely reported in European skies, making it one of the most reported fireball events ever for planet Earth’s American Meteor Society and the International Meteor Organization . The meteor’s measured track over Germany is consistent with its origin near the active radiant of November’s Northern Taurid Meteor Shower , a shower associated with dust from Encke’s comet . Tomorrow’s picture: witch sky? item.title: NASA Awards Moon Base Transportation, Technology, Science Projects
item.description: Artist’s concept of living and working at Moon Base. Credit: NASA NASA announced a suite of awards and mission updates on Saturday to expand the agency’s Moon Base exploration, science, and infrastructure capabilities. The investments will advance commercial robotic deliveries, a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE, launch and orbital transfer services, and surface infrastructure as the agency works with American industry to establish a sustained presence on the Moon’s South Pole. The agency shared the news at the MAX POWER aerospace expo and air show at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. “We are building the Moon Base mission by mission,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Today’s announcements expand nearly every part of that campaign, using the playbook that carried NASA through its greatest eras: fly often, learn, apply those lessons, and get more better and more capable with every mission. When our astronauts return to the Moon, they will arrive with the first elements of the Moon Base already waiting for them on the surface.” “In the eight months since Ignition, we’ve made incredible strides in accomplishing the near impossible: establishing a permanent outpost on the lunar surface,” said Carlos García-Galán, manager, Moon Base Program. “We’ve consolidated numerous efforts into a streamlined program, evolving our human exploration architecture into an iterative and sustained campaign for Moon Base technology development and implementation. Most importantly, we’ve taken action, awarding new contracts and forging new partnerships to accelerate development.” Moon Base cargo landers To strengthen the cargo lander network needed to support the Moon Base, NASA selected eight companies for the next phase of its CLPS ( Commercial Lunar Payload Services ) initiative. The companies are eligible to compete for future lunar surface delivery missions under the new CLPS 2 contract: Blue Origin Firefly Aerospace Intuitive Machines ispace-U.S. Lockheed Martin Space Northrop Grumman Space Systems SpaceX Voyager Technologies Under the CLPS 2 framework, the companies will provide lunar delivery services, including managing, building, and operating landers that transport NASA science, technology, and infrastructure payloads to the Moon. The CLPS 2 framework is a 10-year, multiple-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity master contract with a combined maximum value of $10 billion. NASA increased the value of the current CLPS 1.0 contract from $2.6 billion to $4.2 billion to support initial Phase One Moon Base objectives. The original CLPS contract will remain in place through November 2028, with an additional five-year period to complete awarded lunar deliveries through November 2033. Nuclear-powered Moon rover NASA also announced it is moving forward with development of PROMISE (Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration) . item.title: NASA Seeks Next Generation of Explorers to Join Astronaut Corps
item.description: NASA announced its 2025 Astronaut Candidate Class on Sept. 22, 2025, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credit: NASA/Helen Arase Vargas NASA is looking for the explorers who will help write the next chapter of human spaceflight. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before. U.S. citizens interested in joining the astronaut corps have until 11:59 p.m. EST Thursday, Dec. 3, to submit their completed application materials at: https://go.nasa.gov/3WyvlQi “This is an extraordinary time to join NASA’s astronaut corps,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars. Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage. NASA’s astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation. If you are ready to join that tradition, come help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure.” NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training as the next class of astronaut candidates. “The window is open. The mission is waiting. And the only thing missing from the greatest adventure humanity has ever embarked upon is you,” said NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson. The agency last opened applications in 2024. From more than 8,000 applications, 10 astronaut candidates were selected in 2025 and are currently completing nearly two years of training. “For those who apply, becoming a NASA astronaut is more than a career opportunity,” said Scott Tingle, chief astronaut and chair of the Astronaut Selection Board at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. “It is a chance to join a legacy of explorers who have pushed the boundaries of discovery and play a role in the missions that will shape humanity’s future in space. The next generation of astronaut candidates could help write history while inspiring future scientists, engineers, and explorers.” Since the 1960s, NASA has selected 370 people to train as astronaut candidates for its increasingly challenging missions. The agency has 32 astronauts active in the astronaut corps, and selected applicants will join their ranks to study spacewalking, lunar geology, operations of high-performance aircraft, and more. The basic requirements to apply include United States citizenship and a master’s degree in a STEM field, including engineering, biological science, physical science, or computer science from an accredited institution. item.title: “When Are You Coming Home?” ValueJet Restores Daily Flights to Asaba Ahead of the Festive Season
item.description: Daily Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja services resume on Friday, 20 November 2026, strengthening regional connectivity and bringing families together for the holidays. Somewhere in Lagos or Abuja right now, a phone is ringing, and the voice on the other end is asking the single question that marks the true beginning of the Nigerian festive season: “When are you coming home?” For thousands of professionals, business owners, and families whose answer is Asaba and the surrounding communities across Delta and Anambra states, ValueJet has delivered timely news. The airline will officially resume daily scheduled flights on its Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja routes starting Friday, 20 November 2026, just as year-end travel planning reaches peak momentum. The end of the year carries an undeniable emotional pull back to one’s roots. It is the season of growing gift lists, overpacked suitcases, group chats buzzing with reunion itineraries, and the quiet warmth of returning to familiar streets. For many families, December represents the single period in the year when loved ones assemble under one roof. By reintroducing daily non-stop frequency on both routes, ValueJet provides critical operational flexibility for holiday travelers. Whether passengers are heading home early to spend the entire season with family or flying out closer to Christmas Eve after wrapping up the work year, the restored schedule ensures seamless travel options tailored to diverse holiday schedules. “The festive season is fundamentally about people, relationships, and shared moments. At ValueJet, our mission is to ensure that distance never stands in the way of those connections,” said Omololu Majekodunmi , Managing Director of ValueJet. “Restoring our daily services to Asaba reflects our deep commitment to serving the travel needs of our passengers during the most important time of the year. We are proud to offer a reliable, comfortable, and affordable gateway home for families and communities across the region.” The Lagos–Asaba service bridges Nigeria’s commercial capital directly with the vibrant heart of Delta State, facilitating easy access across the South-South and South-East regions. Simultaneously, the Asaba–Abuja route delivers a direct, hassle-free link between the nation’s capital and Asaba, eliminating lengthy road journeys and complex connection itineraries. The resumption complements ValueJet’s rapidly expanding domestic and regional network. Domestically, the airline provides essential air links to key destinations including Port Harcourt, Jos, Owerri, Calabar, Benin, and GWI-Iperu. Beyond Nigeria’s borders, ValueJet continues to extend its reach beyond established destinations like Accra, Banjul, Cotonou, and Malabo with upcoming regional route expansions to Libreville, Monrovia, and Abidjan. Robots have, and always will, be the first to go to the dark and scary places in space. For many years, Jim oversaw these missions for NASA as their Chief Scientist. He has always been passionate about NASA's science programs and believes we're quite likely to find life off-Earth in the near future. Join us! On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
item.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Fireworks says you’re wasting money on AI unless you’re using all the models
item.description: Fireworks AI is fine with helping companies run AI models in their own datacenters, though VP Rob Ferguson argues against doing so. Ferguson told The Register in an interview that while Fireworks AI, a managed inference provider, supports on-prem AI, "we're trying to push people more and more away from it because frankly, it's just the economics." The GPU hardware is just so expensive that if you can't keep it fully utilized, it's a waste of money, he contends. Ten thousand GPUs, he said, represent a billion dollars of capital. "You don't want those things to be sitting idle," he said. For companies with particularly sensitive workloads, Ferguson said, Fireworks is happy to work something out – it offers a service called Sovereign for just that purpose and it has partners like Microsoft that can help. But most inference work probably doesn't need that level of protection, he said. "The state of the art for everyone is to have a portfolio of models," he explained. "In fact, I think most people don't know that the best model in the world's not Astra. The best model in the world's not Fable. The best model is literally a portfolio and we can prove it. You are always better routing between a few models than to do one singular model." That's what Fireworks does through Nexus and its API, alongside competitors like Together AI, Baseten, and DeepInfra. As a managed inference platform, Fireworks AI routes inference tasks to whichever model, frontier model subscription, or API is best suited to handle them. But the company is not just doing naive routing like an AI gateway. It's evaluating tasks as they come in and directing them to the optimal model. "We build custom routers," Ferguson explained. "Our auto model is continuously updating so that we actually go through and we grade the difficulty of the task and we see if there're affinities that the models have, like Kimi is slightly better at JavaScript than Python, things like this." The company's competitive edge, he contends, is its crack engineering team, which follows from its founders' work on PyTorch, a widely used open source machine learning library. "We're performance experts both on the training and inference side," he explained. "People I think don't understand how important, for example, numerics is. So when you use a model, it's always called a mixture of experts – an expert is a different machine. "And so you have all these different machines. It actually matters when you're training that you go back to precisely the right machine, because if you don't, the other machine will still answer the question, but it'll answer in a slightly different way. So we have to know how to build the topology to write back the data to the right space. We have to understand floating point precision [to handle very small values]. We have to be able to do all this where we're routing through a complex fabric through potentially more than one provider depending on what everything is. And so we're really systems

item.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
item.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." item.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
item.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . Now this is podracing! (Image credit: Secret Mode) A Burnout-inspired Star Wars racer (created by a bunch of ex-Burnout devs) is a fantastic pitch if you know your video games, but looking at EA's recent and current direction, it's easy to see why it didn't happen under their reign. The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day. The not-so-secret sauce, however, was its runs-based structure, which injects the flexibility and replay value of roguelite games into the more traditional arcade racing structure that older gamers are familiar with. (Image credit: EA) Fully confident in its central gameplay idea and devoid of modern live-service baggage, Fuse Games' debut title makes the most of the Star Wars setting within the restrictions of simply making a fun and engaging Star Wars racer. It's almost the same approach we felt in Zero Company, a turn-based tactical strategy-RPG that comes from the minds of another team of ex-triple-A developers. "Star Wars but XCOM" should've happened earlier, but we're glad it did this year, and, unsurprisingly, it's a banger. The correct read of their success should be obvious (and so far, it appears the powers that be are seeing it): Let seasoned and fresh developers cook games they're excited about. Big, medium, or small, players will react positively to experiences that really feel genuine and aren't brought down by tacked-on systems or monetization. item.title: The Bantu expansion changed Africa. Scientists are still tracing how.
item.description: It’s not easy to extract iron from its ore. But the peoples of the ancient city of Great Zimbabwe—the capital of a thriving kingdom in southern Africa between 1000 to 1700 AD—were masters. At sites near the city’s stone ruins, clusters of iron-smelting furnaces survive today as mounds of rubble. At Mashava, a village 25 miles northwest, fragments bear fingermarks of those who long ago smoothed the structures’ clay interiors. Some of the furnaces were nearly an adult’s arm span in width, with walls thick and strong to contain the heat of more than 2,100° Fahrenheit needed to smelt iron. Unlike other furnaces that required workers to force air into them with bellows, these were designed to suck air in, then out through a chimney, no human labor required. This would have made it significantly easier to produce the iron, which was fashioned into hoes, axes, and arrowheads. Read full article Comments

item.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
item.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed. "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. What I care about is that we are launching big rockets no less than once a year," he said. "I think that's imperative for NASA to be doing these deep-space human spaceflight missions right now," Isaacman added. "So, we had a great mission in April of '26. We will launch again in '27." That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. "We need to continue to exercise those muscles," he said, referring to SLS liftoffs. "And, honestly, once a year isn't great, either. I mean, I don't think we're going to get back to the early [space] shuttle days, you know, four missions a year. I don't think we're going to get back to where we were with Apollo, but once a year is the minimum … I would testify that to Congress in this role years down the road. "If NASA is going to be doing deep-space missions, complicated missions, [we should] launch at least once a year and get as much out of it as you can for taking the risk and spending the taxpayer dollars and building towards something greater," Isaacman added. "That's what we're doing with Artemis III, and that's what's going to better prepare us for Artemis IV." A new space race So, how is NASA coping with the challenges that face them as they approach Artemis III ahead of a crewed lunar landing on Artemis IV, which is targeted for 2028? While NASA can learn some lessons from past moon missions with Apollo, today it's primarily relying on the extensive experience and talent within the agency, according to Isaacman. "Artemis II is very different from Apollo 8, and Artemis III will be very different from Apollo 9," he said. "Our approach is not exactly the same as it was … But what is the same right now?
